cues.en: Okay. First, let's get something out of the way. Because this isn't confusing enough, games as a service is not the same as a game service.
cues.zh: 好。首先，先把一件事说清楚。因为这事还不够让人困惑，游戏即服务并不等同于游戏服务。

cues.en: A game service is usually a rental system. So if you pay a company $20 a month and can rent games or have them stream to you, but you can also buy them outright somewhere,
cues.zh: 游戏服务通常是一种租赁系统。所以如果你每月付给某公司20美元，就能租游戏或让它们串流给你，但你也可以在其他地方直接买断，

cues.en: then that's not what I'm talking about. That's not fraud. That's fine.
cues.zh: 那这不是我要说的。那不是欺诈。那没问题。

cues.en: But games as a service, how do we define that?
cues.zh: 但游戏即服务，我们怎么定义它？

cues.en: Well, it's a business practice, but what?
cues.zh: 嗯，它是一种商业行为，但具体是什么？

cues.en: Well, if you're a gamer, you probably have an idea of what it is. So let's list some common traits and see if we can narrow it down to what actually defines it.
cues.zh: 嗯，如果你是个玩家，你大概对它是什么有个概念。那我们来列一些常见特征，看看能不能缩小到真正定义它的东西。

cues.zh: 这是我的清单。我们逐条来看。

cues.en: Online only.
cues.zh: 仅在线。

cues.zh: 是的。我觉得这一条定义了游戏即服务的每一种用法。

cues.zh: 现在有些游戏有可离线运行的下载内容

cues.en: but that's not what the industry means when they refer to this.
cues.zh: 但业界提到这个时，指的不是那个。

cues.en: In fact, another term for games as a service is live service games.
cues.zh: 事实上，游戏即服务的另一个说法是实时服务游戏。

cues.en: In other words, you're connected online so it's live.
cues.zh: 换句话说，你在线连接，所以它是实时的。

cues.en: But hey, I'll give another freebie.
cues.zh: 不过嘿，我再送一个。

cues.en: If offline games as a service games exist,
cues.zh: 如果存在离线的游戏即服务游戏，

cues.en: then those are not fraud.
cues.zh: 那那些不是欺诈。

cues.en: So hey, Oblivion Horse Armor, not fraud.
cues.zh: 所以嘿，Oblivion Horse Armor，不是欺诈。

cues.en: This is actually a great baseline if you wanna determine how fair or not you think I'm being game companies.
cues.zh: 如果你想判断你觉得我对游戏公司有多公平，这其实是个很好的基准。

cues.en: This says something about where my standards are these days.
cues.zh: 这说明我现在的标准处在什么水平。

cues.en: But back to defining things, we'll say yes.
cues.zh: 但回到定义上，我们会说：是。

cues.en: Every games as a service is online only.
cues.zh: 所有游戏即服务都只在线提供。

cues.en: However, not every online game is games as a service.
cues.zh: 不过，并非所有在线游戏都是游戏即服务。

cues.en: We'll come back to that in a minute. Extra online features.
cues.zh: 这个我们稍后再讲。额外的在线功能。

cues.en: This is stuff like stat tracking, matchmaking,
cues.zh: 比如数据统计、匹配，

cues.en: player messaging and so on. Well, games as a service usually have these but they're by no means a guarantee.
cues.zh: 玩家消息等等。游戏即服务通常有这些，但它们绝不是必备保证。

cues.en: Plus regular games can have these too.
cues.zh: 而且普通游戏也可以有这些。

cues.en: Player messaging and voice chat go way back. Stat tracking certainly happened in offline games.
cues.zh: 玩家消息和语音聊天由来已久。数据统计当然也出现在离线游戏里。

cues.en: Matchmaking was usually third party software in the past so I think it's safe to say none of those define games as a service.
cues.zh: 过去匹配通常是第三方软件，所以可以说这些都不能定义游戏即服务。

cues.en: Microtransactions.
cues.zh: 微交易。

cues.en: And you may not believe this but no,
cues.zh: 你可能不信，但不是，

cues.en: those are not what define games as a service.
cues.zh: 这些并不是游戏即服务的定义。

cues.en: Here are a few games as a service that had no microtransactions
cues.zh: 这里有几个游戏即服务，它们没有微交易

cues.en: whatsoever.
cues.zh: 完全没有。

cues.en: However, I will say the overwhelming majority of games as a service do have microtransactions
cues.zh: 不过我得说，绝大多数游戏即服务确实有微交易

cues.en: and this is the number one reason companies
cues.zh: 而这是公司

cues.en: really like this practice.
cues.zh: 真正喜欢这种做法的最主要原因。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 不过，

cues.en: since exceptions do exist,
cues.zh: 既然确实存在例外，

cues.en: this is not actually what defines it.
cues.zh: 这其实并不是它的定义。

cues.en: Subscription fees.
cues.zh: 订阅费。

cues.en: Very few games still have these, so no.
cues.zh: 现在很少有游戏还收这个，所以不是。

cues.en: However, we have that trick again.
cues.zh: 不过，我们又用上了那个套路。

cues.en: Most games as a service do not have a subscription fee,
cues.zh: 大多数游戏即服务没有订阅费，

cues.en: but all games with a subscription fee are games as a service.
cues.zh: 但所有收订阅费的游戏都是游戏即服务。

cues.en: Get it?
cues.zh: 懂了吗？

cues.en: Frequent updates.
cues.zh: 频繁更新。

cues.en: Well, a lot of good games as a service have these, but again, it's by no means what defines them. Plenty of games as a service go by years with no updates at all. So nope, that's not it either.
cues.zh: 很多优秀的游戏即服务确实有这些特征，但这绝不是它们的定义。很多游戏即服务好几年都不更新一次。所以不对，也不是这个。

cues.en: And massive multiplayer games.
cues.zh: 还有大型多人在线游戏。

cues.en: Nope, still not it. On one hand, you have some games as a service that are intended for a small number of players.
cues.zh: 不对，还不是。一方面，有些游戏即服务是面向少数玩家的。

cues.en: On the other hand, you've had some gigantic games that are not this practice.
cues.zh: 另一方面，有些巨型游戏并不属于这种模式。

cues.en: The multiplayer mod for Just Cause two has had over 1,800
cues.zh: 《正当防卫2》的多人模组曾有过超过1800

cues.en: simultaneous
cues.zh: 同时

cues.en: players in the game,
cues.zh: 在线玩家，

cues.en: yet it is not considered games as a service.
cues.zh: 但它并不被视为游戏即服务。

cues.en: MMO games are usually games as a service,
cues.zh: MMO游戏通常是游戏即服务，

cues.en: but not what defines it. Okay. So wow. The only definition that survived is games as a service are online only, and even that one has a caveat.
cues.zh: 但这并不是它的定义。好吧。哇哦。唯一幸存下来的定义是：游戏即服务是仅在线游戏，就连这个定义也有附加条件。

cues.en: See, some games are just meant to be played online.
cues.zh: 你看，有些游戏本来就只适合在线玩。

cues.en: If you play the game Star Siege Tribes,
cues.zh: 如果你玩《星际围攻：部落》，

cues.en: the only way to really play it is to connect to other people. In essence, it's an online only game.
cues.zh: 唯一真正的玩法就是连上其他人。本质上，它是仅在线游戏。

cues.en: Yet, it is not games as a service. You know why?
cues.zh: 然而，它并不是游戏即服务。你知道为什么吗？

cues.en: Because you're still the one in control.
cues.zh: 因为控制权仍然在你手里。

cues.en: Games as a service means the company is providing you the service of allowing you to play your game.
cues.zh: 游戏即服务意味着公司在为你提供服务，允许你玩你的游戏。

cues.en: And yes, I am being facetious.
cues.zh: 是的，我是在讽刺。

cues.en: You didn't used to need permission for that.
cues.zh: 以前你玩这个可不需要许可。

cues.en: Now people will debate what games as a service should mean but this is the real world hard definition.
cues.zh: 现在人们会争论游戏即服务应该是什么意思，但这是现实世界中的硬性定义。

cues.en: Games as a service means the business practice of players not having control of whether they can play a game due to a company withholding that function.
cues.zh: 游戏即服务意味着这样一种商业做法：玩家无法控制自己能否玩一款游戏，因为公司扣着这个功能不放。

cues.en: That is all it is in its purest most distilled
cues.zh: 这就是它最纯粹、最精炼的

cues.en: form.
cues.zh: 形态。

cues.en: Oh, sure. They usually have other stuff on this list but none of those other traits could survive the definition test.
cues.zh: 哦，当然。这个清单上通常还有别的东西，但其他那些特征都通不过定义测试。

cues.en: In fact, I'd say this definition isn't even the intent of games as a service but it is what defines it. If it doesn't have this, it is not games as a service.
cues.zh: 事实上，我会说这个定义甚至不是游戏即服务的初衷，但它正是界定游戏即服务的东西。如果没有这一点，它就不是游戏即服务。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.zh: 欺诈时间到了。

cues.zh: 所以现在我们有了游戏即服务的具体定义。

cues.en: But why is it fraud?
cues.zh: 但为什么说是欺诈？

cues.en: Well, the simplest answer is it's being sold as something it's not.
cues.zh: 嗯，最简单的答案是，它被当成某种它并不是的东西来卖。

cues.en: I'll break it down. But first, we have to understand the difference between a good and a service.
cues.zh: 我来拆解一下。但首先，我们得理解商品和服务之间的区别。

cues.en: Products are defined
cues.zh: 产品被定义为

cues.en: services or goods.
cues.zh: 服务或商品。

cues.en: A good is something you buy and own.
cues.zh: 商品是你购买并拥有的东西。

cues.en: A service is an action performed for you. So if you buy a hammer,
cues.zh: 服务是为你执行的行为。所以如果你买一把锤子，

cues.en: it's a good. It's a thing.
cues.zh: 它是商品。它是个东西。

cues.en: It's yours.
cues.zh: 它归你所有。

cues.en: But if you get a haircut, that's a service. They didn't just hand you your haircut in a box, they used scissors to deliver the desired result or so I'm told.
cues.zh: 但如果你去理发，那就是服务。他们不是把你的发型装进盒子里递给你，而是用剪刀交付你想要的结果——至少别人是这么告诉我的。

cues.en: And again, I have to rail on Wikipedia here.
cues.zh: 而且，我又得吐槽 Wikipedia 了。

cues.en: Since they define goods as something tangible, then later say they're not always tangible.
cues.zh: 因为他们把商品定义为有形的东西，后面又说它们不总是有形的。

cues.en: Good job contradicting
cues.zh: 干得好，这就叫

cues.en: yourself in the first sentence, guys. Whatever. That second part is correct. So things like digital movies you buy are intangible goods.
cues.zh: 第一句就自相矛盾，伙计们。随便吧。第二部分是对的。所以像你买的数字电影这类东西，是无形的商品。

cues.en: You can't touch a movie but it's still sold like a physical good. Well, guess what? Most games are goods too.
cues.zh: 你摸不到电影，但它仍然像实体商品一样出售。好吧，你猜怎么着？大多数游戏也是商品。

cues.en: Even games as a service.
cues.zh: 甚至是服务型游戏。

cues.en: So yes,
cues.zh: 没错，

cues.en: I just said games as a service are not services.
cues.zh: 我刚才确实说了，服务型游戏并不是服务。

cues.zh: 这个我稍后会细说。

cues.en: A license is a right to use a property or intellectual property that belongs to somebody else.
cues.zh: 许可证（license）是指使用归他人所有的财产或知识产权的权利。

cues.en: When you read this software is licensed not sold in a software end user license agreement,
cues.zh: 当你在最终用户许可协议中读到“本软件仅许可使用而非出售”时，

cues.en: The software intellectual property is licensed not sold.
cues.zh: 软件知识产权是许可使用，不是出售。

cues.en: The license is sold not licensed or leased.
cues.zh: 许可协议是出售的，不是许可或租赁的。

cues.en: A little confusing there but let's keep going. All the mass produced items you've bought follow the same rules. You are purchasing a one off copy of the intellectual property of those things and there is a transfer of ownership over those instances
cues.zh: 这里有点绕，但我们继续。你买的所有批量生产的物品都遵循同样的规则。你购买的是这些东西知识产权的一次性副本，并且这些实例的所有权发生了转移

cues.en: and you become the sole owner of that instance of intellectual property.
cues.zh: 你就成为该知识产权实例的唯一所有者。

cues.en: You own it and have full property rights over it. Okay. Just so everybody's with me, he's saying if you buy a copy of
cues.zh: 你拥有它，并对它拥有完整的财产权。好。让大家跟上，他说如果你买了一份

cues.zh: 《半条命》，

cues.zh: 你并不拥有《半条命》系列的权利。

cues.zh: 你不能额外出售它的副本。但你确实拥有你那份《半条命》。

cues.en: A lot of goods are like this. If you buy a car,
cues.zh: 很多商品都是这样。如果你买了一辆车，

cues.en: you don't own the manufacturing
cues.zh: 你并不拥有该车型的制造

cues.en: and design rights to that car model but you do own your car.
cues.zh: 和设计权，但你确实拥有你的车。

cues.en: It's a basic concept.
cues.zh: 这是个基本概念。

cues.en: I said before I'm going up against the narrative.
cues.zh: 我之前说过，我是在对抗一种叙事。

cues.en: Well, one myth you hear sometimes is you don't own any of your software.
cues.zh: 嗯，你有时会听到的一个迷思是，你不拥有任何软件。

cues.en: What he's doing here is explaining why that's almost always false.
cues.zh: 他在这里做的是解释为什么这几乎总是错的。

cues.en: Turns out you have ownership rights after all. Who knew?
cues.zh: 原来你终究是有所有权的。谁知道呢？

cues.en: Next he says there are two types of software licenses,
cues.zh: 接下来他说软件许可证有两种类型，

cues.en: perpetual and subscription licenses.
cues.zh: 永久许可证和订阅许可证。

cues.en: Perpetual ones last forever.
cues.zh: 永久许可证永久有效。

cues.en: So that copy of Mega Man that your brother has in the attic, that's a perpetual license.
cues.zh: 所以你兄弟阁楼里那份《洛克人》，就是永久许可证。

cues.en: And this is why World of Warcraft gets a free pass for now. They want $15 a month. That's as clear as day a subscription license.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么《魔兽世界》目前可以豁免。他们每月要15美元。这明摆着就是订阅许可证。

cues.en: If you're not paying a subscription fee for your game,
cues.zh: 如果你的游戏不是按订阅方式付费的，

cues.en: then it's being bought under a perpetual license.
cues.zh: 那它就是以永久许可证的形式购买的。

cues.en: That's a really key point. A whole lot of things are gonna come back to this.
cues.zh: 这点非常关键。后面很多事情都会回到这一点上。

cues.en: A perpetual license is a product and whenever it's sold it undergoes transfer of ownership upon the point of sale.
cues.zh: 永久许可证是一种产品，每次出售时，在销售的那一刻就发生了所有权转移。

cues.en: Ownership is what establishes one's decision making authority over the thing.
cues.zh: 所有权确立了一个人对该事物的决策权。

cues.en: To sell something is to relinquish it as one's property and to relinquish all of one's decision making authority over that thing to the person who bought it. Then the seller no longer has any rightful say over anything regarding that instance of software represented by its perpetual license.
cues.zh: 出售某物就是放弃它作为自己的财产，并把对该事物的所有决策权让渡给购买它的人。之后，卖方对于该永久许可证所代表的那个软件实例就不再拥有任何正当的发言权。

cues.en: So there it is. If you only have to pay once and it's not a subscription fee for your game,
cues.zh: 所以就是这样。如果你的游戏只需付一次费，而不是订阅费，

cues.en: then by definition it's being sold under a perpetual license.
cues.zh: 那么按定义，它就是以永久许可证的形式出售的。

cues.en: Under most countries' laws, that means it's a good and not a service.
cues.zh: 在大多数国家的法律下，这意味着它是商品，而不是服务。

cues.en: This is why I wonder if games as a service is a deliberate propaganda term.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么我怀疑“游戏即服务”是一个刻意的宣传术语。

cues.en: It means the exact opposite of what it says.
cues.zh: 它的含义和字面意思恰恰相反。

cues.en: But I know what you're thinking. You're thinking this is just some guy on the internet saying words. That doesn't prove anything.
cues.zh: 但我知道你在想什么。你在想这不过是网上某个人在说说而已。那证明不了什么。

cues.en: this is potentially a dangerous precedent, and hey congress, why don't you do something about this? But even then, that decision was just for the Ninth Circuit states, not the entire US.
cues.zh: 这是一个潜在的危险先例，嘿，国会，你们为什么不对这个做点什么？但即便如此，那个裁决也只适用于第九巡回法院辖区，不是整个美国。

cues.zh: 我所说的“杀死游戏”，是指公司采取某些行动，让一款游戏变得完全无法游玩，

cues.zh: 即使是购买过它的人也无法游玩。这也叫作让游戏“变砖”。

cues.zh: 好吧，杀死游戏和游戏即服务是紧紧绑在一起的。

cues.en: If a 100% of all copies sold of a game cease to function because of deliberate interference from the seller after the point of sale,
cues.zh: 如果一款游戏售出的所有副本100%因为卖家在售后的故意干预而停止运行，

cues.en: how can that be considered an honest practice?
cues.zh: 那怎么能被认为是诚实的行为？

cues.en: Now the opposition would say this isn't fraud because you were sold a perpetual license.
cues.zh: 反对者会说这不构成欺诈，因为你买的是永久许可证。

cues.en: And just because the company breaks your game, it doesn't mean you lost your license.
cues.zh: 而且，就算公司弄坏了你的游戏，也不代表你就失去了许可证。

cues.en: You are still free to repair the game after they break it.
cues.zh: 他们弄坏游戏之后，你仍然可以自由修复它。

cues.en: I say this is a disingenuous argument on multiple levels.
cues.zh: 我认为这种论点在多个层面上都站不住脚。

cues.en: If somebody sells you a bike and then later you get a flat tire, yes, your product no longer works and it takes some effort to repair it. But that's something the average person can be reasonably expected to do or hey, take it to a repair shop.
cues.zh: 如果有人卖给你一辆自行车，后来你的轮胎瘪了，没错，你的产品不能用了，修复它需要花点功夫。但这是普通人按理说能做到的事，或者干脆送去修车店。

cues.en: More importantly,
cues.zh: 更重要的是，

cues.en: the company that sold you the bike didn't come to your house and puncture the tire.
cues.zh: 卖你自行车的那家公司并没有跑到你家把轮胎扎破。

cues.en: I see that as an important distinction.
cues.zh: 我觉得这是一个重要的区别。

cues.en: Now when a game as a service stops working, which again I wanna emphasize is a deliberate act,
cues.zh: 那么，当一款游戏即服务停止运行时——我要再次强调，这是蓄意行为——

cues.en: no one on earth could be reasonably expected to fix that.
cues.zh: 地球上没有人能被合理地期望去修复它。

cues.en: The reason for that is twofold.
cues.zh: 原因有两点。

cues.en: First, it takes specialized programming knowledge in order to recreate the portions of the server that were lost.
cues.zh: 第一，重建丢失的服务器部分需要专业的编程知识。

cues.en: Again, the way these games work is most of the data is customer's computer but the company hosting the game has key information about how to run it, where things spawn, logic routines and so on. If you want, you can almost think of this as the body and this as the brain.
cues.zh: 再说一遍，这类游戏的运作方式是：大部分数据在玩家的电脑上，但托管游戏的公司掌握着如何运行游戏的关键信息，比如东西在哪里生成、逻辑例程等等。你可以把这想象成身体，而这个是大脑。

cues.en: When they shut the brain down here, a large portion of the game is now missing and it's unplayable.
cues.zh: 当他们把这里的大脑关掉，游戏的大部分内容就缺失了，变得无法游玩。

cues.en: In order to run the game again, the person would have to write a new brain, I mean, server. Now that is an exorbitant amount of work and takes a lot of specialized knowledge.
cues.zh: 想要再次运行这款游戏，你就得重新写一个大脑——我是说，服务器。这工作量极其庞大，而且需要大量的专业知识。

cues.en: I would estimate only 5% of the population is even capable of doing that.
cues.zh: 我估计全人口里只有 5% 的人能做到这一点。

cues.en: However, it is possible.
cues.zh: 不过，这起码还是可能的。

cues.en: Whether that's a reasonable expectation of buyers to repair their product is debatable.
cues.zh: 但要求买家自己去修产品是否合理，这就有待商榷了。

cues.en: I think it isn't but that is nothing compared to the next part. Programming a new server is difficult enough but companies will also encrypt their data in order to protect against hackers and piracy.
cues.zh: 我觉得很不合理，但跟接下来的问题相比，这都不算什么。写个新服务器已经够难了，厂商往往还会对数据加密，用来防范黑客和盗版。

cues.en: This is known as digital rights management or DRM.
cues.zh: 这就是所谓的数字版权管理，即 DRM。

cues.en: Well, that's reasonable while the product is still being sold but once it's shut down then this is the equivalent of locking things up and throwing away the key.
cues.zh: 游戏还在销售时这样做倒无可厚非，可一旦停服，这就等于把东西锁起来还把钥匙扔了。

cues.en: I've talked to a developer for a resurrected game server emulator and he said they had a cryptography expert helping them decrypt the code and even then, it took them years.
cues.zh: 我曾和一个致力于复活停服游戏的服务端模拟器开发者聊过，他说当时甚至有密码学专家帮他们解密代码，即便如此，还是耗费了数年时间。

cues.en: So if you are qualified to crack codes like what the Nazis were using and win World War two in Europe, then yes, you might be qualified to repair
cues.zh: 所以，如果你有能力破译纳粹当年用的密码、打赢二战欧洲战场，那没准你确实有资格修复

cues.en: your game.
cues.zh: 自己的游戏。

cues.en: I'm really not exaggerating.
cues.zh: 我真的一点都没夸张。

cues.en: Not only is that such a small percentage of the population capable of doing that, but even for them, that in no way can be considered reasonable.
cues.zh: 不仅只有极少数人具备这种能力，而且即便对他们而言，这种要求也绝称不上合理。

cues.en: For most people, I'm talking 99.9%
cues.zh: 对绝大多数人——也就是 99.9%

cues.en: or more, it is impossible
cues.zh: 甚至更多的人来说，

cues.en: for them to repair their game after shutdown.
cues.zh: 在停服之后去修复自己的游戏是完全不可能的。

cues.en: So not literally impossible but again, I'm rounding.
cues.zh: 所以并不是字面意义上的不可能，但再说一次，我是在取整。

cues.en: But let's try to shore this up a little legally.
cues.zh: 但让我们试着在法律层面稍微加强一下这个说法。

cues.en: And again, The United States is hard mode.
cues.zh: 再说一次，美国是困难模式。

cues.en: Some of you may have heard of the term planned obsolescence.
cues.zh: 你们有些人可能听说过“计划性淘汰”这个词。

cues.en: That's the practice of designing goods to intentionally break faster in hopes that you'll buy a new one so they can make more money.
cues.zh: 就是故意设计商品让它更快坏掉，指望你去买新的，这样他们就能赚更多钱。

cues.en: Best I can tell, this is perfectly legal in The United States unfortunately.
cues.zh: 据我所知，不幸的是，这在美国完全合法。

cues.en: But there's a subset of that called programmed
cues.zh: 但其中有一个子集叫做程序化

cues.en: obsolescence.
cues.zh: 淘汰。

cues.en: See, unlike planned obsolescence which just increases the odds the product will break over time,
cues.zh: 你看，计划性淘汰只是增加了产品随时间损坏的几率，

cues.en: programmed obsolescence
cues.zh: 而程序化淘汰

cues.en: ensures
cues.zh: 确保

cues.en: it will break on purpose usually at a specific time.
cues.zh: 它会故意坏掉，通常是在特定时间。

cues.zh: 目前不清楚这在美国是否合法。已经有一些相关案件了，比如2008年Jackie Blenis诉HP的集体诉讼。

cues.zh: 惠普否认有任何不当行为，却给了投诉人500万美元

cues.en: of credit to shut them up.
cues.zh: 的信用额度来堵他们的嘴。

cues.zh: 是啊。我确信他们那么做只是出于好心。

cues.zh: 否则，他们为什么不抗争到底、坚持自己的清白呢？

cues.zh: 因为更新打印机固件来停止接受第三方墨盒。

cues.zh: 换句话说，破坏功能。

cues.zh: 这一次，他们被判有罪，不得不支付150万美元。

cues.zh: 这两起案件都暗示，如果受到挑战，计划性淘汰可能是不合法的。

cues.en: However, in both cases, the reasoning behind the charges doesn't tie directly to that.
cues.zh: 然而，在这两起案件中，指控背后的推理并不直接与此相关。

cues.en: So these aren't the strongest legal precedents in my opinion.
cues.zh: 所以在我看来，这些并不是最有力的法律先例。

cues.zh: 我找到的最有力的法律论据是在2017年的Impression诉Lexmark案中。最高法院裁定，你对自己的产品拥有所有权，可以随心所欲地处置它，

cues.zh: 虽然说计划性淘汰不合法还是有点牵强，

cues.en: isn't legal, I thought these lines from the ruling were noteworthy. Even if the restrictions in Lexmark's contracts with its customers were clear and enforceable under contract law,

cues.zh: 而且专利法没有为限制产品的使用和享用提供任何依据。

cues.zh: 这可能是一个关键句子。

cues.en: There might be something there.
cues.zh: 这里面可能有些门道。

cues.en: But this hasn't been tested in court so most of this is in a legal gray zone.
cues.zh: 但这还没有在法庭上经过检验，所以大部分都处于法律灰色地带。

cues.en: That means the law hasn't specifically said if something is legal or not so everybody has to guess based on other laws.
cues.zh: 这意味着法律并没有明确说明某件事到底合不合法，所以所有人都只能根据其他法律去猜测。

cues.en: I'm obviously on the this is fraud side
cues.zh: 我显然站在“这就是欺诈”这一边

cues.zh: 那一定是有什么东西出问题了。

cues.zh: 你拥有你的游戏吗？

cues.zh: 理论上，

cues.en: yes.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.zh: 严格来说，你永远不会失去那份永久许可的所有权。它是你的。

cues.en: In practice,
cues.zh: 但在实践中，

cues.en: unclear.
cues.zh: 说不清。

cues.zh: 目前还没有更高一级的法院裁定“游戏即服务”是否侵犯了你的永久许可。

cues.en: This is what I'm trying to change.
cues.zh: 这正是我想要改变的。

cues.en: In real world terms, also known as the only part I actually care about,
cues.zh: 用现实世界的说法——也就是我唯一真正关心的部分——

cues.zh: 不，你没有。如果公司把产品停用之后，正常人根本不可能再使用它，那无疑是实质上的所有权丧失。

cues.zh: 时间点移除功能，而且数据还经过加密，防止你自己恢复。

cues.en: It doesn't get any more deliberate to remove your ownership than that. Games as a service is a situation where the outcome is the exact opposite of the intent of the law.
cues.zh: 没有什么比这更蓄意剥夺你的所有权了。“游戏即服务”就是一种结果与法律意图截然相反的情况。

cues.en: This is why the myth that you don't own your games keeps persisting.
cues.zh: 这就是“你并不拥有你的游戏”这种说法一直挥之不去的原因。

cues.en: People are just saying what they're seeing with their own eyes.
cues.zh: 人们只是把自己亲眼所见说出来罢了。

cues.en: Laws are meaningless if they're not enforced.
cues.zh: 法律如果不被执行，就毫无意义。
