cues.en: Every other service I can think of has at least one of the following conditions.
cues.zh: 我能想到的其他所有服务，至少满足以下条件之一。

cues.en: One, an expectation of how long it lasts. If you pay an electric bill, it's usually for a month at a time. Or if you go to an amusement park, your ticket lasts the day or the season. The point being everybody knows when the service is over and it ends or you have to renew it.
cues.zh: 第一，对时长有预期。付电费通常是按月付。去游乐园，门票管一天或一季。重点是大家都知道服务什么时候结束，要么到期，要么得续费。

cues.en: Two, there's a general expectation of when it's done. If you pay roofers to fix your roof, you may have no idea how long that will take but you know when it's fixed. There's a rough idea of when the service is finished.
cues.zh: 第二，对完成时间有大致预期。你雇人修屋顶，可能不知道要修多久，但你知道什么时候算修好。服务何时完成有个大致概念。

cues.en: Three, there are real world limitations
cues.zh: 第三，维持服务存在现实限制

cues.en: towards keeping the service going.
cues.zh: 来让服务持续下去。

cues.en: Some services can go on forever.
cues.zh: 有些服务可以永远持续。

cues.en: If I rent a plot of land,
cues.zh: 如果我租一块地，

cues.en: I don't have to do anything but collect my money each month pretty much. Hence number one here. In fact, I've had a landlord before where at one point I wasn't sure if he was alive or dead but the service kept going.
cues.zh: 基本什么都不用做，每月收租就行。所以就有了第一条。其实我以前有个房东，有段时间我都不确定他是死是活，但服务照常继续。

cues.en: But most services require real resources to continue.
cues.zh: 但大多数服务都需要真实资源才能持续。

cues.en: If you go to a concert and you're having a good time and just wanna stay,
cues.zh: 如果你去听演唱会，玩得正开心，只想留下来，

cues.en: well that's great but the band has to stop sometime.
cues.zh: 那很好，但乐队总得停。

cues.en: Eventually, they're gonna run out of coke.
cues.zh: 最终，他们的可乐会喝完。

cues.en: Maybe you can stump me but I couldn't think of one service that didn't require at least one of those conditions
cues.zh: 也许你能难倒我，但我想不出有哪个服务不需要至少满足其中一个条件

cues.en: except
cues.zh: 除了

cues.en: games as a service.
cues.zh: 游戏即服务。

cues.en: Hence, even on a conceptual level, they're not services.
cues.zh: 因此，即使在概念层面上，它们也不是服务。

cues.en: Here, I'll show you. Expectation
cues.zh: 我来给你演示。预期

cues.en: of how long it lasts.
cues.zh: 它能持续多久。

cues.en: Well, subscription games like World of Warcraft,
cues.zh: 像《World of Warcraft》这样的订阅制游戏，

cues.en: yes, they win this round too. Damn it.
cues.zh: 对，它们这轮也赢了。该死。

cues.en: Subscription games really are services and they're not fraud.
cues.zh: 订阅制游戏确实是服务，也不是骗局。

cues.en: I'll have to get them on the final round.
cues.zh: 我得在最后一轮拿下它们。

cues.en: So besides those few games that still require a monthly fee to play,
cues.zh: 所以除了那几款仍需按月付费才能玩的游戏，

cues.en: no. This doesn't apply.
cues.zh: 不。这条不适用。

cues.en: If there's an expectation for how long games as a service last,
cues.zh: 如果对游戏即服务的持续时长有预期，

cues.en: then what is it? The Culling two lasted a week and a half.
cues.zh: 那是什么？The Culling 2 只持续了一周半。

cues.en: Meridian fifty nine has been going on over twenty two years.
cues.zh: Meridian 59 已经运营超过二十二年了。

cues.en: That's no help. What do the games themselves tell you? Well, most don't tell you anything. They just say they can be shut down at any time for any reason. Some say they can be shut down at any time plus thirty days.
cues.zh: 这没用。游戏本身告诉了你什么？嗯，大多数什么都没说。它们只是说可以随时以任何理由关停。有些说可以随时关停，再加三十天。

cues.en: Even then, I'd argue nobody buying the game is actually expecting it to stop working after thirty days.
cues.zh: 即便如此，我认为买游戏的人没人真的预期它三十天后就不能玩了。

cues.en: Now I'd say there's no standard here but that's not true. There is a standard for games.
cues.zh: 现在我会说这里没有标准，但事实并非如此。游戏是有标准的。

cues.en: The traditional standard is forever.
cues.zh: 传统标准是永久。

cues.en: There are people who speedrun Super Mario Brothers.
cues.zh: 有人速通《超级马里奥兄弟》。

cues.en: That game's over 30 years old.
cues.zh: 那游戏都30多年了。

cues.en: So yeah, forever. That's a good standard.
cues.zh: 所以没错，永久。这是个好标准。

cues.en: Games as a service is trying to push a new standard except it doesn't have one, just that it's less for you.
cues.zh: 游戏即服务想推行新标准，但它根本没有标准，只是让你得到更少。

cues.en: Oh, except for the Secret World and Fallout 76.
cues.zh: 哦，除了《秘密世界》和《辐射76》。

cues.en: They're both saying you'll be able to play them forever.
cues.zh: 它们都说你能永远玩下去。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好吧。

cues.en: Well, for every other game as a service that doesn't last forever,
cues.zh: 那么，对于其他所有无法永久持续的游戏即服务，

cues.en: this is a concrete example of how your rights are being taken away from you. We've gone from play forever to whatever the seller feels like.
cues.zh: 这就是你的权利被剥夺的具体例子。我们从“永久游玩”变成了“卖家想怎样就怎样”。

cues.en: So no, this does not apply.
cues.zh: 所以不，这不适用。

cues.en: Expectation of when it's done.
cues.zh: 关于“什么时候算玩完”的预期。

cues.en: Yeah. Let me ask you, when is somebody done with a game?
cues.zh: 对。我问你，什么时候算某人玩完了一款游戏？

cues.en: When they beat it? What if they wanna play it again?
cues.zh: 通关的时候？那他们想再玩呢？

cues.en: What if it's a game that has no ending? It's just sort of an ongoing thing.
cues.zh: 如果是个没有结局的游戏呢？就是个持续进行的东西。

cues.en: What if they wanna come back and play it after a few years?
cues.zh: 如果他们想几年后回来再玩呢？

cues.en: Exactly. There's no standard at all here.
cues.zh: 没错。这里根本没有任何标准。

cues.en: Well, no. That's not right either.
cues.zh: 不。那也不对。

cues.en: There is a standard for games.
cues.zh: 游戏是有标准的。

cues.en: The old standard used to be that you own the game so you decide when you're done with it. And that's gonna be different for every person.
cues.zh: 旧标准是你拥有游戏，所以由你决定什么时候玩完。这对每个人来说都不一样。

cues.en: So no general standard.
cues.zh: 所以没有通用标准。

cues.en: Real
cues.zh: 现实

cues.en: world limitations.
cues.zh: 世界的限制。

cues.en: Okay. Let me explain this one. Remember that body and brain analogy I made to the server and clients earlier?
cues.zh: 好。让我解释一下这个。还记得我之前把服务器和客户端比作身体和大脑吗？

cues.en: Well, the vast majority of video games throughout history have been sold with both the body and the brain. You got the whole package
cues.zh: 历史上绝大多数电子游戏在售卖时都同时包含身体和大脑。你拿到了完整套装

cues.en: so you could keep the game running as long as you want it. Now with the server and client model, they're set up so that the brain here needs maintenance by real people and computer hardware and electricity bills and so on. But that's a choice,
cues.zh: 所以只要你想，就能让游戏一直运行。现在有了服务器和客户端模式，它们的设置是这里的大脑需要真人维护、计算机硬件、电费等等。但那是一种选择，

cues.en: not a necessity.
cues.zh: 不是必然。

cues.en: See, at their core, video games are code.
cues.zh: 你看，电子游戏的核心就是代码。

cues.en: They're numbers.
cues.zh: 它们就是数字。

cues.en: They don't wear out over time.
cues.zh: 它们不会随时间损耗。

cues.en: The number three works just as well now as it did thousands of years ago. It just looks a little different.
cues.zh: 数字 3 现在和几千年前一样好用，只是样子有点不同。

cues.en: The containers that hold the data can wear out but they can also be copied from one container to the next. So there's an infinite supply.
cues.zh: 承载数据的容器会损耗，但也能从一个容器复制到另一个容器。所以供应是无限的。

cues.en: Don't worry. We're not gonna run out of numbers. They're always on tap.
cues.zh: 别担心，数字不会用完。它们随时可用。

cues.en: Now the server is usually maintained like a service while it's running but once it's shut down,
cues.zh: 服务器运行时通常像服务一样维护，但一旦关停，

cues.en: it could just be copied over here and someone else could get it running.
cues.zh: 它就可以直接复制到这里，别人也能把它跑起来。

cues.en: Companies almost never do that but the point is the limitation isn't real. It's artificial.
cues.zh: 公司几乎从不这么做，但关键在于这个限制并不真实，是人为的。

cues.en: Somebody made it up. They could just as easily undo it.
cues.zh: 有人编造了它，他们也能轻易取消它。

cues.en: In fact, it's easier to undo this rather than set this split up in the first place.
cues.zh: 事实上，取消它比当初设立这种分割更容易。

cues.en: Again,
cues.zh: 再说，

cues.en: most games don't even have this limitation.
cues.zh: 大多数游戏根本没有这种限制。

cues.en: It's not a perfect analogy but imagine a natural park.
cues.zh: 这个类比不完美，但想象一座自然公园。

cues.en: You may pay to go there as a service and there will be people maintaining the roads and trails,
cues.zh: 你可能付费去那里，作为一种服务，还会有人维护道路和步道，

cues.en: running a visitor center, etcetera, and that takes real resources.
cues.zh: 运营游客中心等等，这需要真实资源。

cues.en: But if the park runs out of money and shuts down,
cues.zh: 但如果公园没钱了并关闭，

cues.en: the park doesn't cease to exist.
cues.zh: 公园并不会不复存在。

cues.en: The trees are still there.
cues.zh: 树木还在。

cues.en: The mountains and rocks are all still there.
cues.zh: 山脉和岩石也都还在。

cues.en: We don't erect an indestructible
cues.zh: 我们不会竖起一个坚不可摧的

cues.en: dome around the park that allows nothing in or out and could survive a direct missile strike and then tell everyone with a lifetime pass that they can never enter the park again.
cues.zh: 罩住公园、什么都进不去也出不来的穹顶，还能扛住导弹直击，然后告诉所有持终身通行证的人，他们再也不能进公园了。

cues.en: But that's almost exactly how games as a service works.
cues.zh: 可这几乎就是游戏即服务的运作方式。

cues.en: This is not a good standard.
cues.zh: 这不是个好标准。

cues.en: Hope one of these analogies is sticking.
cues.zh: 希望这些类比里有一个能让你记住。

cues.en: Anyway, the point to all that is that even without the law telling us what's what, games as a service are really not services.
cues.zh: 总之，这一切的重点是，即使没有法律来界定什么是什么，游戏即服务其实根本不是服务。

cues.en: They're goods. So they should be treated as such.
cues.zh: 它们是商品。所以就该被当作商品对待。

cues.en: But hey, maybe you're saying they're a weird exception and should still be treated as services.
cues.zh: 但你可能会说，它们是个奇怪的例外，还是应该被当作服务对待。

cues.en: Okay. Why?
cues.zh: 好吧。为什么？

cues.en: I usually look at the law and rules from the perspective of what's the actual outcome.
cues.zh: 我通常从实际结果的角度来看待法律和规则。

cues.en: Well, the end outcome of most games as a service is that they're destroyed and can never be played again.
cues.zh: 大多数游戏即服务的最终结果就是它们被销毁，再也无法游玩。

cues.en: Jeez, that seems like a really high price to pay to treat them as services.
cues.zh: 天哪，把它们当作服务对待的代价似乎太高了。

cues.en: Now you might be thinking, well, yeah, that sucks but then we also get anti cheat measures, stat tracking, matchmaking,
cues.zh: 现在你可能在想，是啊，这很糟，但我们也能得到反作弊措施、数据统计、匹配系统、

cues.en: easy updates and...
cues.zh: 便捷更新还有……

cues.en: That's the narrative talking.
cues.zh: 那是话术在说话。

cues.en: We can still have all that stuff
cues.zh: 我们仍然可以拥有所有这些

cues.en: and not destroy the game.
cues.zh: 而不摧毁游戏。

cues.en: The narrative likes to frame it like you can't have the good without the bad.
cues.zh: 话术喜欢把它框定成你不能只要好的不要坏的。

cues.en: That's what's known as a false dichotomy
cues.zh: 这就是所谓的假两难

cues.en: and it's just wrong.
cues.zh: 而且它根本就是错的。

cues.en: It's like how you can simultaneously
cues.zh: 就像你可以同时

cues.en: before the circus coming to town but against clown stabbing people.
cues.zh: 期待马戏团来城里，又反对小丑捅人。

cues.en: I know that sounds impossible to some people but it's not that hard a concept.
cues.zh: 我知道这对某些人来说听起来不可能，但这概念没那么难。

cues.en: Companies don't have to give up anything while they're supporting the game.
cues.zh: 公司在支持游戏期间不必放弃任何东西。

cues.en: It's only once they shut the game down that they need to stop treating them like a service and give the customers their goods.
cues.zh: 只有当他们关停游戏时，才需要停止把它们当作服务，把商品还给客户。

cues.en: Now you might be thinking, yeah, but that's probably a bunch of work. Right? Well, it can be but I'm not an expert. So I talked to someone who is.
cues.zh: 你可能会想，是啊，但这大概得花不少功夫吧？对吧？嗯，可能是，但我不是专家。所以我去找了个专家聊了聊。

cues.en: I asked that developer who worked on a server emulator how much work would it take for companies to provide the bare minimum
cues.zh: 我问那位做过服务器模拟器的开发者，公司要提供最起码的东西得花多少功夫

cues.en: to give users a reasonable
cues.zh: 让用户有合理的

cues.en: chance
cues.zh: 机会

cues.en: to create a server emulator once the game shuts down.
cues.zh: 在游戏关服后做出服务器模拟器。

cues.en: Well, he said there were two basic options.
cues.zh: 他说基本有两种方案。

cues.en: I'm not even gonna go over these but you can see them here. Now this would not be enough for a playable game. This would be more like those repair notes like it was mentioned in those European planned obsolescence laws.
cues.zh: 我就不细讲了，你可以在这儿看到。这些还不够做出能玩的游戏。这更像是那些维修说明，就像欧洲计划报废法里提到的那样。

cues.en: But okay, this doesn't seem like too much work so I asked him how long would it take the developers to do this. He said it depended on how well the game was written and how competent the developers are, but anywhere from less than an hour to a few days.
cues.zh: 不过好吧，这看起来工作量不算太大，所以我又问他开发者做这些要多久。他说这取决于游戏写得好不好、开发者能力如何，但少则不到一小时，多则几天。

cues.en: Okay. So now let's compare.
cues.zh: 好。那现在来对比一下。

cues.en: Here are the total pros and cons of having games as a service the way we do it now. Under pros, the developers save anywhere from less than an hour to a few days work. Alright. That's a positive. And under cons, everyone who paid for the game along with anyone in the future interested in the game will never be able to run it again.
cues.zh: 这就是按现在这种方式做游戏即服务的全部优缺点。优点方面，开发者省下了从不到一小时到几天不等的工作量。行，这算个好处。缺点方面，所有买了这游戏的人，以及未来对它感兴趣的人，都再也玩不了了。

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不行。

cues.en: This doesn't seem like a good idea to me. In fact, this looks like a really bad deal for everyone.
cues.zh: 我觉得这可不是个好主意。事实上，这对所有人来说都是笔糟糕的交易。

cues.en: Order for this to be a good deal, I'd say we need a situation like the day after tomorrow where these people are hiding in a library from the worst blizzard ever and need to burn some books so they stay warm and don't die.
cues.zh: 要想让这笔账划算，除非遇到《后天》里那种情况：人们为了躲避史上最强暴风雪躲进图书馆，不得不烧书取暖来保命。

cues.en: See, to me, that looks like a better trade off for destroying media. I'm pretty sure games as a service doesn't save lives.
cues.zh: 你看，在我看来，为了救命而销毁媒介才算说得过去的取舍。而我敢肯定，服务型游戏救不了人命。

cues.en: Now I understand if you think I'm framing this unfairly
cues.zh: 我能理解，你可能会觉得我这么描述有失偏颇，

cues.en: because it sounds kind of crazy that this is the entire reason the industry is defrauding customers and destroying products with millions of dollars and thousands of hours of work behind them. But this is the only honest reason I've seen.
cues.zh: 因为行业欺诈消费者、销毁倾注了数百万美元和成千上万小时心血的产品，全部原因居然只是这个，听起来确实很荒唐。但这也是我见过的唯一真实的理由。

cues.en: It reminds me how in the sixties, auto manufacturers
cues.zh: 这让我想起六十年代，汽车制造商们

cues.en: fought against seat belts being mandatory
cues.zh: 极力反对强制配备安全带，

cues.en: because even though they saved lives, they did cost some money and automakers didn't want that.
cues.zh: 因为尽管安全带能救命，但也确实需要成本，而车企根本不想掏这笔钱。

cues.en: I won't lie. This does cost some money to do but not much at all. I would guess well under 1% of the total budget.
cues.zh: 说实话，做这件事确实要花点钱，但真的少得可怜。我猜远低于总预算的 1%。

cues.en: It's certainly cheaper than making a game a service to begin with.
cues.zh: 肯定比一开始就把游戏做成服务型要便宜得多。

cues.en: So even without the law, if this is the entire reason games are not preserved and customers can never use their products again, I don't find that particularly compelling.
cues.zh: 所以即便撇开法律不谈，如果游戏无法保存、消费者再也无法使用其产品的全部原因仅在于此，我认为这完全站不住脚。

cues.en: It's almost like if there are no laws on this, then there should be.
cues.zh: 这感觉就像是在说：如果在这方面还没有法律，那就真该立一部了。

cues.en: And that brings me to the final argument and this one I can even use on World of Warcraft,
cues.zh: 这就引出了我的最后一个论据，这个论据我甚至可以用在 World of Warcraft 上，

cues.en: finally.
cues.zh: 总算讲到这儿了。

cues.en: Now this may sound crazy considering the first half of this video but I don't actually care about this topic because the industry is breaking the law. That's just a coincidence.
cues.zh: 考虑到这个视频的前半部分，这听起来可能很疯狂，但我其实并不关心这个话题，因为行业正在违法。那只是巧合。

cues.en: I only cover that legal mess because there could be some real power behind that.
cues.zh: 我关注那个法律乱象，只是因为背后可能藏着真正的力量。

cues.en: I think the law is gonna be the only way out of this but that's not my main motivation here.
cues.zh: 我认为法律将是唯一的出路，但那不是我这里的主要动机。

cues.en: No, I care because games as a service is destroying
cues.zh: 不，我在意是因为游戏即服务正在摧毁

cues.en: games.
cues.zh: 游戏。

cues.en: Quite successfully,
cues.zh: 而且相当成功，

cues.en: too.
cues.zh: 真的。

cues.en: Every once in a while, you'll hear people ask if games are art.
cues.zh: 每隔一段时间，就会有人问游戏是不是艺术。

cues.en: I don't have an answer on that, but I think it's pretty clear games are creative experiences
cues.zh: 我对此没有答案，但我认为很明显游戏是创造性的体验

cues.en: often worthy of preservation.
cues.zh: 往往值得保存。

cues.en: So I'll say art just to keep it simple.
cues.zh: 所以为了简单起见，我就说是艺术吧。

cues.en: I mean, come on. If you're looking at stuff like this and are saying no, this has no artistic value at all, you're just being grumpy.
cues.zh: 我是说，拜托。如果你看着这样的东西还说“不，这毫无艺术价值”，那你就是在闹脾气。

cues.en: You know David Bowie's in a game, right?
cues.zh: 你知道David Bowie出现在游戏里吧？

cues.en: Anyway, the point here is that Games as a Service is more than just a consumer rights issue.
cues.zh: 总之，这里的重点是，游戏即服务不仅仅是一个消费者权益问题。

cues.en: Even though the quality ratio is debatable,
cues.zh: 尽管质量比例有待商榷，

cues.en: games contain ideas,
cues.zh: 游戏包含思想、

cues.en: art, often dialogue and ways of interacting that aren't present in any other medium.
cues.zh: 艺术，常常还有对话和互动方式，这些在任何其他媒介中都不存在。

cues.en: They're more than just products.
cues.zh: 它们不仅仅是产品。

cues.en: If I buy a toaster that's designed to fail,
cues.zh: 如果我买了一个设计成会坏掉的烤面包机，

cues.en: well, I still think that's wrong but I can always buy another toaster and still have toast.
cues.zh: 好吧，我仍然认为那是错的，但我总能再买一个烤面包机，仍然有吐司吃。

cues.en: Whereas games are unique experiences.
cues.zh: 而游戏是独特的体验。

cues.en: You can't replace them any more than you can replace books in a library with different authors.
cues.zh: 你无法替换它们，就像你无法用不同作者的书替换图书馆里的书一样。

cues.en: You can't replace Dracula with Twilight
cues.zh: 你不能用《暮光之城》来替代《德古拉》

cues.en: and say nothing was lost because they're both about vampires.
cues.zh: 然后说没什么损失，因为两者都是讲吸血鬼的。

cues.en: It doesn't work that way.
cues.zh: 不是这么回事。

cues.en: I'm not gonna spend much time explaining why saving art has value because for me, it's innate.
cues.zh: 我不打算花太多时间解释为什么保存艺术有价值，因为对我来说，这是本能。

cues.en: If you don't understand why art or creative works have value,
cues.zh: 如果你不理解艺术或创作作品为什么有价值，

cues.en: I probably can't reach you on that. Maybe a philosopher can feel that one.
cues.zh: 我大概没法在这个问题上说服你。也许哲学家能感受到这一点。

cues.en: For me, it's just an instinctive response.
cues.zh: 对我来说，这纯粹是本能反应。

cues.en: Now of course we can't save all artistic works, that's just not practical.
cues.zh: 当然，我们不可能保存所有艺术作品，这不现实。

cues.en: There's too many. Plus, some of them suck.
cues.zh: 太多了。而且，有些确实很烂。

cues.en: But we can decide for ourselves
cues.zh: 但我们可以自己决定

cues.en: what's worth saving and what's not.
cues.zh: 什么值得保存，什么不值得。

cues.en: Games as a service
cues.zh: 游戏即服务

cues.en: denies that chance to everyone.
cues.zh: 剥夺了所有人的这个机会。

cues.en: When I see a game with obvious creative value being destroyed,
cues.zh: 当我看到一款有明显创作价值的游戏被毁掉时，

cues.en: this is what comes to mind.
cues.zh: 我就会想到这个。

cues.en: Now the reality is both better and worse than that.
cues.zh: 现实情况既比那更好，也比那更糟。

cues.en: The part that's better is that games that are destroyed
cues.zh: 更好的部分是，被毁掉的游戏

cues.en: are far less likely to contain ideas that are so powerful,
cues.zh: 远不太可能包含那些如此强大的理念，

cues.en: some see them as a threat.
cues.zh: 以至于有人视其为威胁。

cues.en: The part that's worse is that publishers are way more successful
cues.zh: 更糟的部分是，发行商在毁掉游戏方面

cues.en: destroying games than oppressors ever were at destroying books.
cues.zh: 比压迫者在毁掉书籍方面成功得多。

cues.en: Or, you know, at least within the past few thousand years.
cues.zh: 或者说，至少在过去几千年里是这样。

cues.en: Even at book burning rallies, people didn't burn every existing
cues.zh: 即使在焚书集会上，人们也没有烧掉他们憎恨的书的

cues.en: copy of a book they hated.
cues.zh: 每一个现存副本。

cues.en: And yet, a lot of games as a service have a 100%
cues.zh: 然而，许多游戏即服务有着100%的

cues.en: death rate.
cues.zh: 死亡率。

cues.en: There is no comparison to that in modern media.
cues.zh: 在现代媒体中，这无可比拟。

cues.en: I guess in the early days of film we lost a lot of stuff because the studios didn't know any better. That's what scares me. Now we do know better and yet we're still going backwards.
cues.zh: 我想在电影早期，我们丢失了很多东西，因为制片厂不懂事。这才是让我害怕的。现在我们懂了，却仍在倒退。

cues.en: It's like watching a driver take a bus over a cliff and he knows he's taking it over the cliff. It's a kind of madness.
cues.zh: 就像看着一个司机把公交车开下悬崖，而他知道自己正把它开下悬崖。这简直是一种疯狂。

cues.en: And speaking of modern media, you can rent movies or stream music as a service but you can also
cues.zh: 说到现代媒体，你可以租电影或把音乐流媒体当服务用，但你也可以

cues.en: buy them and keep them as goods.
cues.zh: 买下它们，把它们当作商品留着。

cues.en: I guess some TV shows or radio shows you can't buy but guess what?
cues.zh: 我猜有些电视节目或广播节目买不到，但你猜怎么着？

cues.en: You can back them up yourself,
cues.zh: 你可以自己备份它们，

cues.en: legally.
cues.zh: 合法地。

cues.en: Not to dip back into the law again,
cues.zh: 倒不是又要扯回法律，

cues.en: but that's what this case was all about.
cues.zh: 但这正是本案的关键所在。

cues.en: Technically, it's already legal to back up games as a service in multiple countries,
cues.zh: 严格来说，在多个国家，将游戏备份为服务已经是合法的，

cues.en: even in The USA.
cues.zh: 即使在美国。

cues.en: But if game companies make that impossible,
cues.zh: 但如果游戏公司让这变得不可能，

cues.en: then what does that matter?
cues.zh: 那这有什么关系呢？

cues.en: I care about reality,
cues.zh: 我在意现实，

cues.en: not fantasy rights.
cues.zh: 不是幻想中的权利。

cues.en: I wanna say games as a service are the only form of modern media without real world limitations
cues.zh: 我想说，游戏即服务是现代媒体中唯一不受现实世界限制的形式

cues.en: that you cannot preserve.
cues.zh: 那是你无法保留的。

cues.en: It's kind of amazing in a terrible way.
cues.zh: 从糟糕的角度看，这还挺惊人的。

cues.en: And that's what this all comes down to for me. Even if Games as a Service passed every legal test, which it hasn't,
cues.zh: 对我来说，归根结底就是这样。即便“游戏即服务”通过了所有法律检验，而事实并非如此，

cues.en: then the law would be wrong.
cues.zh: 那这个定律就错了。

cues.en: Games as a Service, the way we do it now,
cues.zh: 游戏即服务，也就是我们现在的做法，

cues.en: permanently destroys games and all the work the creators put into them. It's entirely preventable and serves almost no purpose for anyone.
cues.zh: 会永久摧毁游戏以及创作者投入的所有心血。这完全可以避免，而且对任何人都几乎没有好处。

cues.en: It's just wrong.
cues.zh: 这是不对的。

cues.en: The whole point of laws is to have a more civilized society.
cues.zh: 法律的意义就在于让社会更文明。

cues.en: Wanting destruction of art that others are trying to preserve and have paid for is not civilized.
cues.zh: 想要毁掉别人正努力保存、并且已经花钱买下的艺术品，这不文明。

cues.en: That's why this needs to stop, even for subscription games. We just have to stop it. Stop it. Stop it. Stop
cues.zh: 这就是为什么必须停止，即便是订阅制游戏也一样。我们就是得停下来。停下。停下。停下

cues.en: it. Stop it. Stop it.
cues.zh: 就是它。停下。停下。

cues.en: And that's my case. So I would be almost done, but you know how the Internet is.
cues.zh: 这就是我的论点。所以我本来差不多就讲完了，但你知道互联网是什么样的。

cues.en: Somebody can make a good point, but then somebody else comes along, nitpicks something, and then says, Debunked.
cues.zh: 有人能提出一个很有道理的观点，但马上就会有人跳出来吹毛求疵，然后说：“已被辟谣。”

cues.en: All done.
cues.zh: 全都讲完了。

cues.en: Uh-uh.
cues.zh: 才不是。

cues.en: I mean, that may still happen but I wanna wreck that before it even gets started.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，这种情况可能还是会发生，但我想在它开始之前就彻底击垮它。

cues.en: Now if you're already on board with what I'm saying, you can skip straight to the end.
cues.zh: 如果你已经认同我说的，那可以直接跳到结尾。

cues.en: Yeah. See? There you go. But games as a service is a plague of an idea so I need to burn out every last inch of it I can.
cues.zh: 对吧，看到没？就是这样。但“游戏即服务”这种想法简直就是一场瘟疫，所以我得把能烧掉的最后一寸都烧光。

cues.en: So I'm going into overtime to show just how weak the opposition is.
cues.zh: 所以我要加时，证明反方的论据到底有多薄弱。

cues.en: I think it's so bad it's indefensible.
cues.zh: 我觉得这糟糕到根本无法辩护。

cues.en: But hey, judge for yourself.
cues.zh: 不过，还是你自己判断吧。

cues.en: So here are my rebuttals to every major counter argument or concern I can think of before they happen. Here we go.
cues.zh: 所以，在各种反驳真正出现之前，我先回应我能想到的每一个主要反驳或担忧。开始吧。

cues.en: Let's start with the big one. Games as a service is legal because you agree to the term stated in the end user license agreement.
cues.zh: 先说最重要的一点。“游戏即服务”是合法的，因为你同意了最终用户许可协议中的条款。

cues.en: Well, the simple answer is yes. Those terms apply as long as they don't contradict anything the law says.
cues.zh: 简单说，没错。只要这些条款不违反法律规定，它们就有效。

cues.en: If they say something that is not legal, then those documents mean nothing.
cues.zh: 如果其中写了违法的内容，那些文件就毫无意义。

cues.en: Nothing.
cues.zh: 毫无意义。

cues.en: That's why I spent half the video focusing on the law and almost didn't care what those documents said.
cues.zh: 所以我花了视频一半的篇幅来关注法律，几乎没在意那些文件写了什么。

cues.en: If the law says they're wrong,
cues.zh: 如果法律规定它们是错的，

cues.en: that's all there is to it. It's not even a debate.
cues.zh: 那事情就到此为止了。这甚至都不值得争论。

cues.en: The end user license agreements are irrelevant
cues.zh: 最终用户许可协议与

cues.en: to this conversation.
cues.zh: 这场讨论无关。

cues.en: That's what that Lexmark Supreme Court case was showing. They simply don't determine the law. It's good to think of those agreements like club rules.
cues.zh: 这就是Lexmark最高法院案所揭示的。他们根本不能决定法律。把这些协议想象成俱乐部规则就好。

cues.en: So if you're at the Moose Lodge and the rules say you have to make an antler face before you can speak at the meetings,
cues.zh: 所以如果你在Moose Lodge，规则说你在会议上发言前必须做个鹿角脸，

cues.en: well, then those are the club rules.
cues.zh: 那好吧，那些就是俱乐部规则。

cues.en: You don't actually lose your right to speak.
cues.zh: 你实际上并没有失去发言权。

cues.en: But let's crush this argument a little further.
cues.zh: 但我们再把这个论点深入剖析一下。

cues.en: Maybe you think the law is wrong and the customer assumed the risk of shutdown when they bought the game.
cues.zh: 也许你认为法律是错的，客户在购买游戏时就承担了停服的风险。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好吧。

cues.en: Well then, when was it supposed to shut down?
cues.zh: 那么，它应该在什么时候停服呢？

cues.en: I don't think there's been one case in the history of games as a service where the company told the customer when the game was gonna shut down upon release.
cues.zh: 我认为在游戏即服务的历史上，从来没有一个案例是公司在发布时就告诉客户游戏什么时候会停服。

cues.en: That means the agreements are made in bad faith because the company is purposefully
cues.zh: 这意味着这些协议是恶意制定的，因为公司故意

cues.en: withholding
cues.zh: 隐瞒

cues.en: information from the customer.
cues.zh: 信息，不让客户知道。

cues.en: Now personally, I think that's a weaker argument that doesn't get to the core issue but it's still true.
cues.zh: 个人而言，我认为这是一个较弱的论点，没有触及核心问题，但它仍然是事实。

cues.en: Game shutdowns are not a force of nature.
cues.zh: 游戏停服不是自然力量。

cues.en: They are entirely within the company's control.
cues.zh: 它们完全在公司控制之内。

cues.en: In order to defend the end user license agreement,
cues.zh: 为了捍卫最终用户许可协议，

cues.en: you would have to say that companies are entitled to sell you a product,
cues.zh: 你不得不说公司有权卖给你一个产品，

cues.en: break that product after the point of sale,
cues.zh: 在销售后破坏那个产品，

cues.en: not tell customers when that's going to happen even though it's in their control
cues.zh: 不告诉客户什么时候会发生，即使这在他们的控制之内

cues.en: and then prevent customers from repairing the product after it's broken.
cues.zh: 然后阻止客户在产品损坏后修复它。

cues.en: That is not good business. That is predatory.
cues.zh: 这可不是什么好生意，这是掠夺行为。

cues.en: Good luck defending that.
cues.zh: 祝你能为这种做法辩护成功。

cues.en: Okay. Here's another big one. Buying a game entitles you to the client software.
cues.zh: 好，还有个大问题。买一款游戏意味着你有权获得客户端软件。

cues.en: You are not entitled to the server software.
cues.zh: 但你无权获得服务器软件。

cues.en: Technically,
cues.zh: 严格来说，

cues.en: yes, that is true.
cues.zh: 是的，确实如此。

cues.en: But that's not the whole story.
cues.zh: 但事情没那么简单。

cues.en: Part of what I was trying to show in the legal portion is that there's a precedent, if not laws,
cues.zh: 我在法律部分想说明的一点是，即使没有明确法律，也有先例支持

cues.en: that customers are entitled to a working product
cues.zh: 客户有权获得可正常使用的产品，

cues.en: or a reasonable chance of repairing one. So no, the customer is not entitled to the server software.
cues.zh: 或者有合理的机会去修复它。所以，客户确实无权获得服务器软件。

cues.en: But since they are entitled to a working product,
cues.zh: 但既然他们有权获得可正常使用的产品，

cues.en: that usually means the server software also.
cues.zh: 这通常也意味着要有服务器软件。

cues.en: Doesn't have to. The company could patch the game for it to run offline instead.
cues.zh: 不一定。公司也可以给游戏打补丁，让它离线运行。

cues.en: In fact, I have a really easy test that sums up my whole stance on this.
cues.zh: 其实，我有一个很简单的测试，能概括我对此事的全部立场。

cues.en: Step one, company sells the game.
cues.zh: 第一步，公司卖游戏。

cues.en: Step two, the company conducts business any way they want to.
cues.zh: 第二步，公司想怎么经营就怎么经营。

cues.en: Step three, company support ends. And step four, the customer has a reasonable chance to run the game after shutdown.
cues.zh: 第三步，公司停止支持。第四步，客户在停服后有合理的机会运行游戏。

cues.en: What the company does in step two here is a black box.
cues.zh: 公司在这第二步里做什么是个黑箱。

cues.en: I am in no way trying to dictate how they run their business there. I'm only concerned with step four here. Can the customer run the game?
cues.zh: 我绝不是想规定他们该怎么经营。我只关心这里的第四步：客户能运行游戏吗？

cues.en: In games as a service, the answer is currently no.
cues.zh: 对于游戏即服务，目前答案是不能。

cues.en: This is what it's all about right here.
cues.zh: 这才是问题的核心。

cues.en: Notice it doesn't say release the server software.
cues.zh: 注意，它没说发布服务器软件。

cues.en: It says give the customers a chance to run their game that they paid for. How the company does that is up to them.
cues.zh: 它说的是给客户一个机会，让他们能运行自己花钱买的游戏。公司怎么做，由他们自己决定。

cues.en: In fact, if you get confused by anything I've said in this video and get lost somewhere, just look at that chart. This chart is all you really need to know. Simple.
cues.zh: 其实，如果你被视频里的任何内容搞懵了，看这张图就行。你真正需要了解的就全在这张图上了。很简单。

cues.en: Easy.
cues.zh: 很容易。

cues.en: I guess I should have put that at the beginning.
cues.zh: 我想我应该把它放在片头的。

cues.en: Oops.
cues.zh: 哎呀。

cues.en: What you're proposing would require businesses to support their games forever.
cues.zh: 你的提议相当于要求厂商永远维护他们的游戏。

cues.en: That's unreasonable.
cues.zh: 这太不合理了。

cues.en: No, they wouldn't.
cues.zh: 不，并不用。

cues.en: In fact, I'm in favor of companies ending support for a game any time they want.
cues.zh: 实际上，我非常支持厂商随时终止对游戏的维护支持。

cues.en: That's why an end of life plan is essential.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么“停运过渡方案”至关重要。

cues.en: If you're a company and you end support for your game but then the customer still has a reasonable chance to play it after that, that's it. You're done. You don't have to support anything.
cues.zh: 如果你是一家厂商，停运了游戏，但玩家在那之后依然有合理的途径继续玩，这就行了。你的任务完成了，不需要再维护任何东西。

cues.en: What needs to stop is support being a requirement
cues.zh: 真正需要叫停的，是把官方维护变成

cues.en: to play the game.
cues.zh: 游玩这款游戏的必要前提。

cues.en: That's what games as a service is.
cues.zh: 这才是服务型游戏的问题所在。

cues.en: If games as a service have to be treated as goods, it will hurt creativity of developers and restrain them.
cues.zh: 如果把服务型游戏当作传统商品对待，会扼杀开发者的创造力并束缚他们。

cues.en: Well, first I'd like to point out the industry made games as goods for decades and I didn't see a lot of shortage of creativity myself.
cues.zh: 首先我想说的是，游戏行业把游戏当商品做了几十年，我可没见有多缺乏创造力。

cues.en: And again, we're talking up to a few extra days of work.
cues.zh: 而且说到底，我们讨论的顶多也就几天额外的工作量。

cues.en: I don't see how that would kill creativity
cues.zh: 我完全看不出这怎么就会扼杀创造力，

cues.en: unless the point of the game was for it to die.
cues.zh: 除非这款游戏设计的初衷就是为了消亡。

cues.en: Well, wouldn't you know it, we've had a game just like that, The Flock.
cues.zh: 巧的是，还真有这么一款游戏：The Flock。

cues.en: This was a multiplayer game that the developers actually wanted to die.
cues.zh: 这是一款开发者本来就希望它死掉的多人游戏。

cues.en: After a fixed amount of player deaths, it was going to shut down forever and they told people that right from the beginning.
cues.zh: 在全服玩家累计死亡达到固定次数后，游戏就会永久关服，而且他们从一开始就挑明了这点。

cues.en: Now I would actually allow an exemption for this game because I think there's an argument to be made that this was performance art.
cues.zh: 其实我会给这款游戏开个例外，因为我认为可以说这是一种行为艺术。

cues.en: See, all other games as a service, they don't die because the creators want them to. It happens because they become unprofitable
cues.zh: 你看，其他所有游戏即服务，它们消亡并不是因为创作者希望如此，而是因为变得不盈利了

cues.en: and they handle the shutdowns irresponsibly.
cues.zh: 而他们对关服的处理又不负责任。

cues.en: But this one, game death was the entire
cues.zh: 但这款游戏，游戏死亡本身就是整个

cues.en: point.
cues.zh: 重点所在。

cues.en: So guess what happened?
cues.zh: 所以你猜怎么着？

cues.en: They ran out of money to pay for server hosting so they shut the game down prematurely.
cues.zh: 他们没钱付服务器托管费了，于是提前把游戏关了。

cues.en: So the one game that wanted to die couldn't do it the way it intended.
cues.zh: 所以唯一一款想死的游戏，却没能按它想要的方式死去。

cues.en: Its creative vision was compromised
cues.zh: 它的创作愿景被损害了

cues.en: because of games as a service.
cues.zh: 正是因为游戏即服务。

cues.en: Thus, as far as I know, games as a good has never hurt creativity.
cues.zh: 因此，据我所知，游戏作为商品从未损害过创造力。

cues.en: Let's look at that chart again. Does this chart look like it's strangling creativity?
cues.zh: 再看看那张图。这图看起来像是在扼杀创造力吗？

cues.en: But let's say it somehow was. Is that one game being allowed to die not worth making rules for all others?
cues.zh: 但就算它 somehow 确实如此。难道为了允许那一款游戏死去，就不值得为其他所有游戏制定规则吗？

cues.en: I don't think so.
cues.zh: 我不这么认为。

cues.en: If the law was enforced on games as a service, it would negatively affect a lot of companies that would have to go back and change their games and they may not be able to do that.
cues.zh: 如果对游戏即服务强制执行法律，会对很多公司产生负面影响，它们得回头修改自己的游戏，而它们可能做不到。

cues.en: I consider the current situation so bad that I would accept that any laws on this not apply retroactively.
cues.zh: 我认为现状糟糕到我可以接受任何相关法律不溯及既往。

cues.en: If I can save all the games of the future for the price of a 100 or so games today, that's a devil's bargain I can live with. Now it's not like I have any power to compromise with,
cues.zh: 如果我能用今天大约100款游戏的代价，拯救未来所有的游戏，那这笔魔鬼交易我能接受。不过我也没什么妥协的权力，

cues.en: I'm just talking on a pure conceptual level. I want every base covered.
cues.zh: 我只是在纯概念层面讨论。我想把所有情况都覆盖到。

cues.en: This is such a black and white issue to me. I don't wanna leave any room for people going, oh, it's so hard to come up with a rule for this. I guess it's impossible to do anything about it. No. I want clear rules for any scenario.
cues.zh: 这对我来说是非黑即白的问题。我不想给人留任何余地，让他们说，哦，这太难定规则了。我猜这事没办法处理。不行。我要为任何场景定清晰的规则。

cues.en: In fact, if I miss one, come at me. I'll straighten you out.
cues.zh: 事实上，如果我漏了一条，来找我。我会纠正你。

cues.en: What about free or free to play games?
cues.zh: 那免费游戏或免费游玩游戏呢？

cues.en: Well, if a game is truly free, no money involved, I'd say the law doesn't apply nor should it. That would hurt creativity.
cues.zh: 嗯，如果游戏真正免费，不涉及金钱，我会说法律不适用，也不应该适用。那会伤害创造力。

cues.en: People wanna experiment with concepts and throw bad experiments out sometimes.
cues.zh: 人们想试验概念，有时会把糟糕的试验扔掉。

cues.en: There doesn't need to be a higher responsibility on the person if they're just messing around.
cues.zh: 如果人们只是随便玩玩，就不需要承担更高的责任。

cues.en: It's once they start taking money for that that they're entering legal territory and just a higher responsibility
cues.zh: 一旦他们开始为此收钱，就进入了法律领域，责任也更高了，

cues.en: in general since then their actions start affecting others.
cues.zh: 因为从那时起，他们的行为开始影响他人。

cues.en: Now free to play games, games that are free but you can also buy extra items or features,
cues.zh: 现在说免费游玩游戏，即免费但你可以购买额外物品或功能的游戏，

cues.en: those are easy. Treat them like any other commercial game.
cues.zh: 那些很简单。像对待任何其他商业游戏一样对待它们。

cues.en: If you buy a virtual sword in a game and then the game shuts down so you can no longer access it, it's been taken from you. Your property rights have been infringed upon.
cues.zh: 如果你在游戏中买了一把虚拟剑，然后游戏关闭，你无法再访问它，它就被夺走了。你的财产权受到了侵犯。

cues.en: Hence the need to treat it like the good it is so you can keep what you paid for.
cues.zh: 因此需要把它当作商品对待，这样你才能保留你花钱买的东西。

cues.en: Making a server emulator work on another system is a lot of work. Developers can't be expected to do that. Well, that's why I presented the minimum effort options here. See, the situation is so bad right now I found a way to lower my standards even further. I used to think these were the only ways for a company to not commit fraud for a games as a service shutdown.
cues.zh: 让服务器模拟器在另一个系统上运行是很多工作。不能指望开发者这么做。嗯，这就是我在这里提出最低努力选项的原因。你看，现在情况太糟了，我找到了进一步降低标准的方法。我以前认为这些是公司避免在游戏即服务关闭时构成欺诈的唯一方式。

cues.en: But wouldn't you know it, that minimum effort solution sort of qualifies too.
cues.zh: 但你可能想不到，这个最省事的方案居然也算勉强达标。

cues.en: If a developer provides this, then the game enters possible to repair territory which I still don't think is great but I can live with that. And again, this is anywhere from under an hour to a few days of work.
cues.zh: 如果开发者提供了这个，游戏就进入了“可以修复”的范畴，我依然觉得这不怎么样，但能接受。再说一遍，这大概是不到一小时到几天的工作量。

cues.en: If that is still just too much work for you to handle then you shouldn't be selling games as a service.
cues.zh: 如果这点活儿你都处理不了，那就不该把游戏当服务来卖。

cues.en: Laws enforcing games as goods would negatively affect games that get shut down temporarily
cues.zh: 强制把游戏当商品的法律，会误伤那些临时关服

cues.en: but then come back up.
cues.zh: 但之后又重新上线的游戏。

cues.en: Good point. I agree with you. That's why I think a grace period is quite reasonable.
cues.zh: 说得好，我同意。所以我觉得给个宽限期挺合理的。

cues.en: If a game is shut down for a couple months but then comes right back up so buyers can play it again, that's acceptable.
cues.zh: 如果游戏关服几个月，但之后又恢复上线，让买家能重新玩，那可以接受。

cues.en: I think what the appropriate time period is is debatable.
cues.zh: 具体多长时间合适，我觉得可以讨论。

cues.en: However, I consider never an unacceptable answer.
cues.zh: 但“永远不恢复”我认为不可接受。

cues.en: Requiring companies to give players a chance to play their games upon shutdown is overreach and an infringement on business rights.
cues.zh: 要求公司在关服时给玩家一个继续玩的机会，这是越权，是对经营权的侵犯。

cues.en: The whole idea behind a perpetual software license is the business is giving up a tiny bit of its rights in exchange for money. It's the customer paying the business, not the other way around.
cues.zh: 永久软件授权的核心逻辑是：商家让出一小部分权利来换钱。是客户付钱给商家，不是反过来。

cues.en: What's actually happening is overreach from the business.
cues.zh: 实际发生的是商家在越权。

cues.en: They're trying to take back rights that they sold.
cues.zh: 他们想收回已经卖出去的权利。

cues.en: If I were to sell you a car and then later steal it and drive it back to my lot, we wouldn't say I'm protecting my rights. We would say I robbed you.
cues.zh: 如果我卖给你一辆车，然后又把车偷走开回我的停车场，我们不会说我在保护自己的权利。我们会说我在抢你。

cues.en: You're just being an idealist.
cues.zh: 你不过是个理想主义者。

cues.en: Things break down or go bad all the time. Games are no different. Yes, they are. Video games are code,
cues.zh: 东西总是会损坏或变质的。游戏也不例外。不，它们不一样。电子游戏是代码，

cues.en: numbers.
cues.zh: 是数字。

cues.en: Games are more like stories.
cues.zh: 游戏更像是故事。

cues.en: Books go bad, stories don't unless we let them. Hey, there's this story called The Odyssey.
cues.zh: 书本会破损，故事却不会，除非我们任由它消亡。你看，有个故事叫《奥德赛》（The Odyssey）。

cues.en: It's pretty good. It's about 3,000 years old though it's only been published for twenty four hundred years. When's that one supposed to go bad by?
cues.zh: 它相当精彩。大约有3000年的历史了，虽然出版只有2400年。那它什么时候才会“过期”呢？

cues.en: But you know what? That's not a game. So how about Go?
cues.zh: 但你可能会说，那又不是游戏。那围棋（Go）呢？

cues.en: That one's two and a half thousand years old. People still play it. So no, this doesn't apply to games.
cues.zh: 它有两千五百年的历史了。人们今天依然在下。所以，这套说法根本不适用于游戏。

cues.en: See, I have to point this out because some people just don't get it. Cheese goes bad. Car tires go bad. Math equations
cues.zh: 看吧，我必须把这点指出来，因为有些人就是想不通。奶酪会变质，汽车轮胎会老化，但数学公式

cues.en: do not.
cues.zh: 绝不会。

cues.en: Again, there's a real narrative pushing back against this. Just to pick on someone, take a look at this article. Elliot here argues that all these online games are going to get shut down.
cues.zh: 然而，现实中确实有舆论在反驳这一点。随便举个例子，看看这篇文章。这位名叫 Elliot 的作者声称，所有这些网络游戏终究都会停服。

cues.en: He's right about that. Then he tries to argue that this is welcome and inevitable.
cues.zh: 这一点他确实没说错。但他接着试图论证，这种结局是值得欣然接受且不可避免的。

cues.en: Well, no. That's wrong. He then compares game shutdowns to TV shows ending like Star Trek. I'm guessing if he took a logic class in school, he didn't get top marks.
cues.zh: 才怪，这完全是错的。他甚至把游戏停服比作像《星际迷航》（Star Trek）这样的电视剧完结。我猜他上学时要是上过逻辑课，成绩肯定不及格。

cues.en: See, here's the difference, Elliot. People can still watch those TV shows today because they were preserved.
cues.zh: 你看，区别就在这里，Elliot。人们今天依然能看到那些电视剧，因为它们被保存了下来。

cues.en: If no one today could ever watch Star Trek again,
cues.zh: 如果今天再也没有人能看到《星际迷航》，

cues.en: then yes, that would be a solid analogy.
cues.zh: 那行，你这个类比才算站得住脚。

cues.en: What he's actually arguing here is development and support on a game eventually ends.
cues.zh: 他在这里实际争论的是，游戏的开发与支持终有结束的一天。

cues.en: Yes.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: That's why an end of life plan is necessary.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么需要一个生命周期终止计划。

cues.en: Their shutdown is inevitable.
cues.zh: 它们的关停不可避免。

cues.en: Their destruction
cues.zh: 它们的毁灭

cues.en: is not.
cues.zh: 却并非如此。

cues.en: There are people playing Star Wars Galaxies right now even though that game was officially shut down over seven years ago.
cues.zh: 现在还有人在玩《星球大战：星系》，尽管那款游戏正式关服已经超过七年了。

cues.en: Do you think those people accepted the ending back in 2011?
cues.zh: 你觉得那些人在2011年接受了终结吗？

cues.en: Now that's only possible because a developer illegally leaked code to the game but it just goes to show a game ending is not inevitable at all.
cues.zh: 这之所以可能，只是因为一名开发者非法泄露了游戏代码，但这恰恰说明游戏的终结根本不是不可避免的。

cues.en: Now I don't think Elliot here is a bad faith actor. I think he just doesn't know any better.
cues.zh: 我不认为这里的Elliot是恶意为之。我觉得他只是不懂更好的做法。

cues.en: And it's unfortunate he's also a game journalist
cues.zh: 不幸的是，他还是个游戏记者

cues.en: because then he influences others to buy into the misinformation.
cues.zh: 因为他会影响别人去相信这些错误信息。

cues.en: This is exactly how a constructed narrative works.
cues.zh: 这正是建构式叙事的运作方式。

cues.en: Go read The Odyssey, Elliot. Maybe something will click in your brain.
cues.zh: 去读读《奥德赛》吧，Elliot。也许你脑子里会有什么开窍。

cues.en: What you are proposing is outrageous because it would require companies to give up their intellectual property
cues.zh: 你提出的主张太离谱了，因为这会要求公司放弃他们的知识产权

cues.en: and they cannot release their game without losing their trademark.
cues.zh: 而且他们不失去商标就无法发布游戏。

cues.en: Okay. I pointed out earlier that the perpetual license in no way entitles the buyers to the intellectual property rights.
cues.zh: 好。我前面指出过，永久许可绝不赋予购买者知识产权。

cues.en: All they get is that single instance of it. I was never arguing that rights holders should lose their IP.
cues.zh: 他们得到的只是那一个实例。我从未主张权利持有人应该失去他们的IP。

cues.en: That's actually the whole point. People with perpetual licenses have rights also.
cues.zh: 这恰恰是关键所在。持有永久许可的人也有权利。

cues.en: As for trademark,
cues.zh: 至于商标，

cues.en: companies can still protect their trademark and release an unsupported game.
cues.zh: 公司完全可以在保护商标的同时，发布不再提供支持的游戏。

cues.en: They just have to be in front of it and define the terms.
cues.zh: 他们只需要提前把控，明确好条款就行。

cues.en: As an example, Grand Theft Auto, a commercial game, has been released for free multiple times by Rockstar and they no longer support that game. Do you honestly think Rockstar lost the rights and trademark to the Grand Theft Auto franchise because of that?
cues.zh: 举个例子，商业游戏 Grand Theft Auto 就被 Rockstar 免费发布过多次，而且他们也不再维护那款游戏了。你真觉得 Rockstar 会因此失去 Grand Theft Auto 系列的版权和商标吗？

cues.en: I think they have some money invested into that one.
cues.zh: 我觉得他们在那上面可没少砸钱。

cues.en: Using trademark as an excuse to kill a game means the company is operating irresponsibly.
cues.zh: 拿商标当借口来彻底关停游戏，说明这家公司的运营极其不负责任。

cues.en: That's the point here. If the company wants to solve a problem, they can.
cues.zh: 这才是问题的关键。如果公司真想解决问题，他们是能做到的。

cues.en: If they don't,
cues.zh: 如果不想，

cues.en: there's infinite excuses.
cues.zh: 借口要多少有多少。

cues.en: Not good excuses,
cues.zh: 虽然算不上什么好借口，

cues.en: but excuses nonetheless.
cues.zh: 但终究也是借口。

cues.en: You say games are goods but old arcades were services
cues.zh: 你说游戏是商品，但当年的街机算服务，

cues.en: so there is a historical precedent for this.
cues.zh: 所以这事是有历史先例的。

cues.en: See, I knew you were gonna say that. Well, let's go back to that service list again. With arcades, you had one of these first two criteria.
cues.zh: 看吧，我就知道你会这么说。那我们再回过头看那份服务清单。对于街机，它符合前两条标准中的一条。

cues.en: Maybe you played the game until you died or played until three minutes were up. It depended on the game. And for sure, arcades had real limits.
cues.zh: 要么是你一直玩到命用光，要么是玩到三分钟倒计时结束，这取决于具体游戏。而且毫无疑问，街机受限于现实客观条件。

cues.en: These were machines with space age technology that weighed 300 pounds.
cues.zh: 这些机器重达 300 磅，里面可都是当时的顶尖技术。

cues.en: And hey, if you really wanted to, you could buy the arcade machine as a good and preserve it. Oh, sure. It costs thousands of dollars but that goes back to the real world limits.
cues.zh: 而且，如果你真想的话，完全可以把街机当成商品买回家收藏。当然，这要花上几千美元，但这又回到了现实物理限制的问题。

cues.en: It's just not the same thing at all. In fact, arcade machines only prove the point.
cues.zh: 这根本就不是一回事。事实上，街机恰恰证明了这一点。

cues.en: Arcades
cues.zh: 街机

cues.en: mostly died off but the games survived.
cues.zh: 大多已经消亡，但游戏活了下来。

cues.en: You keep mentioning the law and need for law enforcement but this isn't necessary.
cues.zh: 你一直在提法律和执法的必要性，但这并不必要。

cues.en: Companies just need to be convinced preserving games is in their interest and customers need to make conscientious buying decisions.
cues.zh: 公司只需要被说服，保护游戏符合他们的利益，而消费者需要做出有意识的购买决策。

cues.en: Listen. We tried it your way already. It didn't work. For decades this wasn't an issue for the vast majority of games.
cues.zh: 听着。我们已经试过你的方式了。没用。几十年来，对绝大多数游戏来说这都不是问题。

cues.en: Nobody was enforcing laws on games as a service because almost nobody was doing it. Great.
cues.zh: 没人对“游戏即服务”执法，因为几乎没人这么做。好极了。

cues.en: That's not what's happening now. We're seeing large percentages of blockbuster titles engaged in games as a service.
cues.zh: 现在情况不同了。我们看到大量重磅作品都在搞“游戏即服务”。

cues.en: Why should we try to convince companies not to do something when they're the ones that created the problem in the first place?
cues.zh: 既然是公司自己制造了这个问题，我们为什么还要去说服他们不要这么做？

cues.en: The companies that can be convinced aren't the ones doing this. Remember,
cues.zh: 能被说服的公司恰恰不是在做这件事的那些。记住，

cues.en: this absolute minimum effort solution could take under an hour. But even I have to admit that still takes some effort.
cues.zh: 这个最低限度的方案可能用不了一小时。但连我都得承认，那还是需要花点功夫的。

cues.en: Killing games requires
cues.zh: 杀死游戏只需要

cues.en: no effort.
cues.zh: 毫不费力。

cues.en: I've heard people say before that companies would be happy to preserve games if they could just be convinced that it's more profitable.
cues.zh: 我以前听人说过，只要能让公司相信保护游戏更有利可图，他们会乐意去做的。

cues.en: But you know those people running shell games on the street that are scams?
cues.zh: 但你见过街上那种骗人的猜杯子把戏吗？

cues.en: They're asking you to pick a cup when the ball is actually in their pocket? I'm sure they would be happy to run an honest game if you could convince them that was more profitable than scamming people.
cues.zh: 他们让你猜球在哪个杯子里，其实球就在他们口袋里？我确信，只要你能让他们相信老老实实玩比骗人更赚钱，他们会很乐意公平地玩。

cues.en: But the thing about fraud is that it already has an excellent profit to work ratio,
cues.zh: 但欺诈这件事的好处在于，它的收益与投入之比已经非常出色了，

cues.en: a maximum one even.
cues.zh: 甚至是最高的。

cues.en: Customers are not going to convince companies that honest business is more profitable than fraud because it's usually not.
cues.zh: 顾客无法说服公司，诚实经营比欺诈更有利可图，因为通常并非如此。

cues.en: But I think law enforcement could convince them.
cues.zh: 但我认为执法部门可以说服他们。

cues.en: But hey, prove me wrong. Maybe the industry will see the error of its ways and stop killing games before any of this ever goes to court.
cues.zh: 不过，嘿，证明我错了。也许行业会认识到自己的错误，在这件事上法庭之前就停止扼杀游戏。

cues.en: But do you really wanna bet on the industry policing itself?
cues.zh: 但你真的想赌行业会自我监管吗？

cues.en: Really?
cues.zh: 真的吗？

cues.en: I'll bet against you. Hit me up. My email's at the end of this video.
cues.zh: 我跟你赌不会。联系我。我的邮箱在这段视频末尾。

cues.en: What about streaming only games?
cues.zh: 那纯流媒体游戏呢？

cues.en: Streaming only games are ones you can only play through a video feed. It's the only way.
cues.zh: 纯流媒体游戏是指只能通过视频流播放来游玩的游戏。这是唯一的途径。

cues.en: So forget everything that was shown in that body and brain chart. Streaming only games is like you're watching all that through a window.
cues.zh: 所以忘掉那张身体和大脑图表里展示的一切吧。纯流媒体游戏就像你透过一扇窗户看那一切。

cues.en: You have nothing then.
cues.zh: 那你就什么都没有了。

cues.en: At this point in time, these are mostly prototypes but they're coming.
cues.zh: 目前，这些大多是原型，但它们即将到来。

cues.en: However, it's the same thing as before.
cues.zh: 然而，这和之前是一回事。

cues.en: If they're under a subscription license,
cues.zh: 如果它们是订阅许可下的，

cues.en: then all I have is the preservation argument not to destroy history.
cues.zh: 那我只有保护历史的论点，不能销毁历史。

cues.en: I'm not sure there's any legal standing.
cues.zh: 我不确定这有没有法律依据。

cues.en: But if they're under perpetual licenses and you buy the streaming games,
cues.zh: 但如果它们是永久许可下的，而你购买了流媒体游戏，

cues.en: yep, back to fraud.
cues.zh: 是的，又回到欺诈了。

cues.en: That's why we need to challenge this now before this becomes the norm.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么我们需要现在挑战这一点，趁它还没成为常态。

cues.en: And that also means they'll have to release a lot more than this in order to let customers repair their game after shutdown.
cues.zh: 这也意味着他们必须发布比这多得多的东西，才能让顾客在服务器关闭后修复他们的游戏。

cues.en: You were pushing to enforce laws on games as goods, but won't that lead to companies declaring everything as a service with a subscription fee and getting around it that way?
cues.zh: 你之前主张把游戏当作商品来立法，但这不就会导致公司把一切都声明为服务、收订阅费，从而绕开监管吗？

cues.en: That is a risk, but you know what? We've been there before and saw how it turned out.
cues.zh: 这确实是个风险，但你知道吗？我们以前经历过这种事，也看到了结果。

cues.en: In the early to mid two thousands,
cues.zh: 在两千年代初到中期，

cues.en: almost every mmo game was subscription only.
cues.zh: 几乎所有的MMO游戏都只提供订阅制。

cues.en: Well, guess what happened?
cues.zh: 结果呢？

cues.en: Almost all of them either failed or went to a different payment model.
cues.zh: 几乎所有游戏要么失败了，要么转向了不同的付费模式。

cues.en: Only a few survived on subscription fees.
cues.zh: 只有少数几款靠订阅费活了下来。

cues.en: So if every company goes to a subscription model, most are going to fail because gamers aren't going to be eager to have five different game bills a month.
cues.zh: 所以如果每家公司都转向订阅模式，大多数都会失败，因为玩家不会乐意每个月收到五份游戏账单。

cues.en: I think the economics of this aren't going to work out for companies that do this exclusively
cues.zh: 我认为只做订阅的公司，从经济上是行不通的

cues.en: and they know it.
cues.zh: 而且他们自己也清楚。

cues.en: That's why games as a service exist.
cues.zh: 这就是“游戏即服务”存在的原因。

cues.en: They're pretending to be services
cues.zh: 它们假装是服务，

cues.en: while they're really goods and they're evading the responsibilities
cues.zh: 实际上却是商品，还在逃避

cues.en: of both.
cues.zh: 两边的责任。

cues.en: What about delisted games?
cues.zh: 那下架游戏呢？

cues.en: Delisted games are games you can't buy online anymore or sometimes at all.
cues.zh: 下架游戏就是你没法再在线购买、有时甚至完全买不到的游戏。

cues.en: I have mixed feelings on those.
cues.zh: 我对这事心情复杂。

cues.en: On one hand, I of course want people to be able to play games that they're interested in. On the other hand, I don't think it's reasonable to force companies to sell their games if they don't want to. There's nothing fraudulent about what they're doing so all I have is the preservation argument.
cues.zh: 一方面，我当然希望人们能玩到他们感兴趣的游戏。另一方面，我觉得强迫公司出售他们不想卖的游戏并不合理。他们的做法没有任何欺诈性，所以我唯一的论据就是保存游戏这一条。

cues.en: And again, this comes back to me wanting to stay black and white on this issue and I am laser focused on not killing games.
cues.zh: 话说回来，我还是想在这个问题上泾渭分明，我现在的核心焦点完全在“不要让游戏停服死掉”上。

cues.en: Maybe once we solve that, I can care more about other areas like this.
cues.zh: 也许等我们解决了这个问题，我才有心思去关心类似的其他领域。

cues.en: What about games that are updated all the time so the early version is very different than the later version? Isn't it unreasonable for developers to preserve each version?
cues.zh: 但那些一直在更新、早期版本和后期版本大相径庭的游戏该怎么办？要求开发者保留每一个版本是不是太强人所难了？

cues.en: That could take a lot more work, yes,
cues.zh: 确实，那可能会增加大量工作，

cues.en: which is why I'm willing to compromise on this too.
cues.zh: 所以在这点上我也愿意妥协。

cues.en: I would consider
cues.zh: 我认为，

cues.en: any working version of the game as adequate compensation for the buyer.
cues.zh: 只要能提供任何一个可正常运行的游戏版本，对买家来说就足以算作合理的交代了。

cues.en: Now of course, it'd be nicer to have each version available but again, I wanna leave no excuses
cues.zh: 当然，如果每个版本都能保留自然更好，但我还是不想给厂商留下任何借口，

cues.en: not to provide customers with a working copy of the game. So if the company can only provide one point o and not 3.6,
cues.zh: 让他们推脱不给玩家提供一份可运行的游戏。所以，如果厂商只能提供 1.0 而无法提供 3.6 版本，

cues.en: whatever.
cues.zh: 无所谓。

cues.en: Anything is better than nothing. We're getting way too much nothing right now.
cues.zh: 有总比没有强。我们现在经历的“彻底失去”实在太多了。

cues.en: I don't care if old games aren't preserved because I only play new games.
cues.zh: “我不在乎老游戏保不保留，反正我只玩新游戏。”

cues.en: Fine. Then you shouldn't care if laws get enforced on the old ones. Although sometimes, they're not that old.
cues.zh: 行吧。那针对老游戏的法律哪怕落地执行，你应该也不会介意。虽然有时候，那些游戏其实也没那么老。

cues.en: Anyway, this shouldn't affect you. You can go back to sleep.
cues.zh: 反正这也不会影响到你，你大可接着睡大觉。

cues.en: This guy challenged EA in court on how his games should last longer and lost.
cues.zh: “当年有人因为游戏运营期应该更长而在法庭上硬刚 EA，结果输了。”

cues.en: Therefore, you don't have rights on your games.
cues.zh: “所以，你对自己买的游戏根本没有权利。”

cues.en: This case was arguing the multiplayer portion of his games should last longer and it ended up being sent to arbitration
cues.zh: 那个案子争论的是游戏的多人联机部分应该维持更长时间，而且最后案件被移交给了仲裁，

cues.en: which is notorious for siding with businesses and the records were kept private.
cues.zh: 而众所周知仲裁向来偏向大企业，相关的记录也都被保密了。

cues.en: He could have been arguing the case on completely different grounds than what I've been making that wouldn't hold up in court.
cues.zh: 他本可以拿跟我一直在讲的完全不同的理由来为这个案子辩护，而我一直在讲的那些理由在法庭上站不住脚。

cues.en: We don't know what happened and whatever did happen is not the law of the land.
cues.zh: 我们不知道发生了什么，而且不管实际发生了什么，那都不是现行法律。

cues.en: This is also a perfect example of why legal strategy matters.
cues.zh: 这也是说明法律策略为何重要的绝佳例子。

cues.en: If you go into the wrong court with the wrong argument, you'll lose. I found a ruling in The UK that says perpetual licenses aren't perpetual,
cues.zh: 如果你带着错误的论点走进错误的法院，你就会输。我在英国找到一份裁决，说永久许可证并不是永久的，

cues.en: so you're wrong.
cues.zh: 所以你是错的。

cues.en: First, this was only in The UK.
cues.zh: 第一，这只在英国。

cues.en: Second, the perpetual part was more in reference to its usage in the contract
cues.zh: 第二，所谓“永久”那部分，更多是指它在合同里的使用方式

cues.en: and the fact that it was referring to ten years to begin with means it wasn't a perpetual contract in the first place. So that's just a really odd interpretation that may not apply specifically to software.
cues.zh: 而且它一开始说的就是十年，这说明它本来就不是永久合同。所以那只是一个非常奇怪的解释，可能并不专门适用于软件。

cues.en: Third, the European Union High Court ruling on perpetual licenses supersedes this one. Maybe Brexit will shake things up but even then it will still just be The UK.
cues.zh: 第三，欧盟高等法院关于永久许可证的裁决优先于这一份。也许脱欧会带来变化，但即便如此，那也仍然只是英国。

cues.en: If companies release information about their servers, this means other games they're hosting with the same software could be hacked.
cues.zh: 如果公司公开其服务器的信息，这就意味着他们用同一软件托管的其他游戏也可能被黑。

cues.en: I asked that developer about this and he said in either of these scenarios,
cues.zh: 我问过那个开发者这件事，他说在这两种情形中的任何一种下，

cues.en: this doesn't give a hacker enough information to hack another game that he couldn't get without it anyway.
cues.zh: 这都不会给黑客足够的信息去黑另一款游戏，而这些信息他反正没有它也搞不到。

cues.en: But even if he's wrong, I kind of wanna say too bad,
cues.zh: 但就算他错了，我有点想说：那也没办法，

cues.en: at some point a company should take responsibility
cues.zh: 到了某个时候，公司就该承担责任

cues.en: for its actions
cues.zh: 为自己的行为负责。

cues.en: And that's how I feel about most of these counter arguments.
cues.zh: 这就是我对大多数这些反驳论点的看法。

cues.en: They're excuses.
cues.zh: 这些都是借口。

cues.en: They're excuses not to do what everybody in gaming should know is needed. This right here is not the end of the world.
cues.zh: 这些都是借口，让人不去做游戏界人人都知道该做的事。这还不是世界末日。

cues.en: Somehow, companies found a way to make thousands of games in the past and not destroy them. It's necessary to go back to that.
cues.zh: 不知怎么的，过去公司能找到办法做出成千上万的游戏，还不把它们毁掉。有必要回到那种做法。

cues.en: And it's cheap.
cues.zh: 而且成本很低。

cues.en: See, companies are gonna fight us all the way on this because, you know, customers are the enemy, but this is what they care about.
cues.zh: 你看，公司在这件事上会一直跟我们对着干，因为你知道，客户是敌人，但这才是他们真正在乎的。

cues.en: This is their gravy train and preserving games doesn't need to interfere with that. If I could get companies to understand one thing, it's that this is gonna be way cheaper than any litigation.
cues.zh: 这是他们的摇钱树，而保存游戏并不需要妨碍这一点。如果我能让公司明白一件事，那就是这比任何诉讼都便宜得多。

cues.en: I don't expect them to get that message but I wanted to say it.
cues.zh: 我不指望他们能听懂这个信息，但我想说出来。

cues.en: All I want here is the absolute bare minimum of responsibility
cues.zh: 我在这里只想要绝对最低限度的责任

cues.en: to not kill games. Just the tiniest bit. My god.
cues.zh: 不要杀死游戏。就一点点。天哪。

cues.en: And finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: we're done.
cues.zh: 我们说完了。

cues.en: So what now?
cues.zh: 那现在呢？

cues.en: Well, I didn't make this video for my health.
cues.zh: 嗯，我做这个视频可不是为了自娱自乐。

cues.en: This isn't some TED talk where I say something positive and then everybody acts like the problem solved.
cues.zh: 这不是什么TED演讲，我说点积极的话，然后大家就装作问题解决了。

cues.en: No. I made this to actually get something done.
cues.zh: 不。我做这个是为了真正做点事。

cues.en: At this point, I've taken things as far as I can on my own.
cues.zh: 到了这一步，靠我自己能做的已经到头了。

cues.en: So this video is an SOS for help to take things further.
cues.zh: 所以这个视频是一个求救信号，希望大家帮忙把事情推进下去。

cues.en: If you think you can help with ending this practice, let me know. Here's my email.
cues.zh: 如果你觉得自己能帮忙终结这种做法，告诉我。这是我的邮箱。

cues.en: I probably need people like lawyers or law students,
cues.zh: 我可能需要律师或法学生这样的人，

cues.en: especially in consumer law,
cues.zh: 尤其是消费者法方面的，

cues.en: activist organizers or anyone with connections to organizations
cues.zh: 活动组织者，或者任何有关系能联系到组织的人

cues.en: that could actually get the ball rolling on this.
cues.zh: 真正能让这件事动起来的人。

cues.en: Here, I made cheat sheets of all the important stuff I discussed in the video. I'll make this and key information you might want available as a download link also. I think there might be some meat on some of the legal precedents but we need them to be examined and ruled on. Here's a few more ideas I had about possible places to start.
cues.zh: 我在这里整理了视频中讨论的所有重要内容的速查表。我会把这些以及你可能需要的关键信息做成下载链接提供给大家。我觉得某些法律先例里可能有些有价值的东西，但需要有人去审查和裁决。以下是我关于可能从哪里入手的一些更多想法。

cues.en: And the thing to realize is we don't need to win all battles to win the war.
cues.zh: 需要认识到的是，我们不需要赢得每一场战斗才能赢得整场战争。

cues.en: Say we can't make any progress at all in The United States but we can in the European Union and Australia.
cues.zh: 比如说，我们在美国完全推不动，但在欧盟和澳大利亚可以。

cues.en: Well, that could be enough to make companies had end of life plans globally
cues.zh: 这就足以让公司在全球范围内制定终止支持计划了

cues.en: because then that will be cheaper than facing fines or lawsuits.
cues.zh: 因为那样比面对罚款或诉讼更便宜。

cues.en: Anyway, I don't know what to do with this information, who to contact, what the procedure is. I'm a layman. It's a miracle I was able to put this together as it is.
cues.zh: 总之，我不知道该怎么处理这些信息，该联系谁，流程是什么。我是个外行。我能把这些整理出来已经是个奇迹了。

cues.en: My most valuable function in all this is as a mascot to get people fired up in the right direction.
cues.zh: 在这件事里我最有价值的作用就是当个吉祥物，把人们鼓动到正确的方向上去。

cues.en: Yeah, like that. That could be me.
cues.zh: 对，就是这样。那个人可以是我。

cues.en: Somebody else needs to figure out how to use this. Maybe an agency says they can help but they need enough public interest first?
cues.zh: 需要别人来想办法利用这些。也许某个机构说他们能帮忙，但需要先有足够的公众关注度？

cues.en: Well then, I'll be right back up here telling everybody to contact them. Or, maybe all that's needed is some legal person submitting the right documents to the right offices.
cues.zh: 那我会马上回到这里告诉大家去联系他们。或者，也许只需要某个法律人士把正确的文件提交给正确的部门就行了。

cues.en: I'm trying to pull people out of the ether who have more of a clue how to push this forward than I do. I said at the beginning that I'm declaring war on games as a service.
cues.zh: 我在努力把那些比我更懂怎么推进这件事的人从茫茫人海中拉出来。我在开头就说过，我要对游戏即服务宣战。

cues.en: That's true but this is retaliatory.
cues.zh: 这没错，但这是报复性的。

cues.en: The games industry itself has declared a war on ownership against the consumer for years now and they're winning.
cues.zh: 游戏行业多年来已经对消费者宣战，要剥夺他们的所有权，而且他们正在赢。

cues.en: We're seeing the industry act with utter impunity on this.
cues.zh: 我们看到这个行业在这方面肆无忌惮。

cues.en: At the time of this video, a new era is starting.
cues.zh: 在本视频制作时，一个新时代正在开始。

cues.en: Stadia has been announced with streaming only exclusive games,
cues.zh: Stadia 已宣布推出仅限流媒体的独占游戏，

cues.en: meaning you'll never be able to preserve those. It's impossible.
cues.zh: 意味着你永远无法保存这些游戏。这不可能。

cues.en: Not even that point 1% chance.
cues.zh: 连那百分之一的机会都没有。

cues.en: And they're not alone.
cues.zh: 而且他们不是孤例。

cues.en: So many companies are tripping over themselves to do streaming games just like that.
cues.zh: 很多公司都争先恐后地搞这种流媒体游戏。

cues.en: The games industry is so eager to take away the concept of consumer ownership.
cues.zh: 游戏行业如此急于剥夺消费者所有权的概念。

cues.en: And that means these games are gonna get destroyed.
cues.zh: 这意味着这些游戏会被毁掉。

cues.en: This is like something out of a science fiction story to me. And yet, here we are. Now, I'm as cynical a person as you're gonna find on this topic and even I am seeing a chance to change this.
cues.zh: 这对我来说就像科幻故事里的情节。然而，现实就是如此。现在，在这个话题上，我是你能找到的最愤世嫉俗的人，但连我都看到了改变这一切的机会。

cues.en: The law could be our ally on this. We don't know. The problem is the law has been utterly asleep at the wheel regarding the games industry.
cues.zh: 法律可能是我们的盟友。我们不确定。问题在于，法律在游戏行业方面一直完全失职。

cues.en: So we have to wake the law up. We're gonna lose for sure if it keeps on sleeping.
cues.zh: 所以我们必须唤醒法律。如果它继续沉睡，我们肯定会输。

cues.en: Even if it's against us, there is no downside to getting the law involved.
cues.zh: 即使法律对我们不利，让法律介入也没有坏处。

cues.en: The situation has gotten that bad.
cues.zh: 情况已经糟糕到这种地步了。

cues.en: Because of that, I'm only interested in plans where the end game is some sort of legal process.
cues.zh: 正因为如此，我只对最终走向某种法律程序的计划感兴趣。

cues.en: I think that's our only chance.
cues.zh: 我认为那是我们唯一的机会。

cues.en: I don't think changing consumer habits will work.
cues.zh: 我不认为改变消费习惯会奏效。

cues.en: In fact, I saw a quote before that said something like, anytime someone says the solution to a problem is to vote with your wallet,
cues.zh: 事实上，我之前看到过一句话，大意是：每当有人说解决某个问题的办法是“用钱包投票”时，

cues.en: I know that cause is doomed.
cues.zh: 我就知道这个事业注定要失败。

cues.en: That really reflects my own views as well.
cues.zh: 这也很符合我自己的看法。

cues.en: I think legislation
cues.zh: 我认为立法

cues.en: could work but I also see that as almost impossible.
cues.zh: 或许可行，但我也觉得这几乎不可能。

cues.en: I have no power.
cues.zh: 我没有任何权力。

cues.en: If I was a multi millionaire and could hire lobbyists to push this through congress,
cues.zh: 如果我是个千万富翁，能雇游说者推动国会通过法案，

cues.en: yeah, that could work,
cues.zh: 是的，那或许可行，

cues.en: but that's not me.
cues.zh: 但我不是那样的人。

cues.en: But getting judges somewhere to interpret existing laws?
cues.zh: 但让某些地方的法官去解释现行法律呢？

cues.en: That at least seems possible.
cues.zh: 这至少看起来有可能。

cues.en: I care about games not being killed but I'm not gonna fight this forever. There are other things I'd rather be doing.
cues.zh: 我在乎的是游戏不被“杀死”，但我不打算永远为这件事战斗下去。我还有更想做的事。

cues.en: But I either need this practice to stop or else I need to be defeated.
cues.zh: 但我要么需要这种做法停止，要么就得被击败。

cues.en: I need to have high courts come down and say games will never be protected before I can give this up.
cues.zh: 我需要高等法院下来裁定游戏永远不会受到保护，我才能放弃这件事。

cues.en: This is just phase one, informing people and the SOS for help. Phase two is to wake the law up. We need knowledgeable people for that part.
cues.zh: 这只是第一阶段——让大众知情并发出求救信号。第二阶段是唤醒法律。这部分需要有专业知识的人参与。

cues.en: Now if you wanna help but don't have any particular knowledge on this, well then you're in the same boat I am. We're just gonna have to wait and see who reaches out.
cues.zh: 现在，如果你想帮忙但对这方面没有任何专业知识，那你其实和我的处境一样。我们只能等着看谁会站出来。

cues.en: Believe me, I'll let you know if we need your help.
cues.zh: 相信我，如果我们需要你的帮助，我一定会告诉你。

cues.en: In the meantime, the only advice I have is making noise on this certainly won't hurt.
cues.zh: 在此之前，我唯一的建议是：在这件事上发声肯定不会有坏处。

cues.en: Just getting gamers to understand that they legally do own their games isn't a bad start.
cues.zh: 让玩家明白他们在法律上确实拥有自己的游戏，就是一个不错的开始。

cues.en: I'm still impressed by that post explaining it and you're welcome to use my chart. It's nice and simple.
cues.zh: 我仍然对那篇解释它的帖子印象深刻，也欢迎你使用我的图表。它简单明了，挺好的。

cues.en: In fact, you can take anything I've said in this video and use it however you want. That's fine. Maybe more noise will help, maybe it won't matter. That's large scale zeitgeist manipulating stuff. I don't know how to do that. I'm single issue here. Stop killing games.
cues.zh: 事实上，你可以随意使用我在这段视频里说的任何内容。没关系。也许更多噪音会有所帮助，也许根本无所谓。那是大规模操纵时代思潮的东西。我不知道该怎么做。我这里只关心一件事：别再扼杀游戏。
